title: Attributing compound flood impact from tropical cyclone Idai in Mozambique to climate and population change
abstractText: Abstract Impacts of extreme weather events are a complex interplay of compounding climatic and socio-economic drivers. In this paper, we attribute the effect of climate and population change on the number of people exposed to flooding from tropical cyclone (TC) Idai, making landfall in Mozambique in 2019. We apply an extended storyline attribution framework based on a globally-applicable model chain to simulate compound flooding and exposed population as a proxy for impact under factual and counterfactual climate and population conditions. This enables impact attribution to both drivers, and disaggregation across flood depth categories and socio-economic groups. Under the selected storyline experiments, 84% of the exposed population is attributable to the combined effect of climate and population change since 1975, with population change alone accounting for 80% and climate change alone for 9%. Climate change increases flood extent and flood depth, whereas population change alters the number of people living in the flooded area. These drivers change the distribution of people exposed to flooding, leading to different attribution assessments per flood depth category. Our results indicate that the effect of climate change is not evenly distributed across socio-economic groups, which is masked when spatially aggregating the attribution assessment.

title: Residual meniscal extrusion was not associated with 2-year clinical outcomes after posterior lateral meniscus root repair in a cohort predominantly undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
abstractText: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: The clinical significance of residual meniscal extrusion after posterior lateral meniscus root repair, particularly with concomitant anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction, remains uncertain. This study evaluated longitudinal clinical and imaging outcomes after transtibial pull-out repair of traumatic posterior lateral meniscus root tears and examined whether residual extrusion was associated with the final Lysholm score or change from baseline at 2-year follow-up. METHODS: Thirty patients with arthroscopically confirmed traumatic posterior lateral meniscus root tears underwent transtibial pull-out repair and completed 2-year follow-up; 28 underwent concomitant ACL reconstruction. Lysholm scores were obtained preoperatively and at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Residual extrusion was measured once on 1.5-T magnetic resonance imaging at 24 months. Associations of extrusion with the postoperative score and score change were assessed using Spearman correlation. A sensitivity analysis was restricted to patients with concomitant ACL reconstruction. RESULTS: [4] = 120.0; p < 0.0001; Kendall W = 1.00). Twenty-nine patients (96.7%) reported returning to their preinjury recreational sport. Mean residual extrusion was 2.06 ± 0.51 mm. Extrusion was not statistically significantly associated with the 24-month Lysholm score (Spearman ρ = -0.13; 95% confidence interval, -0.48 to 0.25; p = 0.495) or change from baseline (ρ = 0.18; p = 0.340). Results were similar in the sensitivity analysis of the 28 patients with concomitant ACL reconstruction. CONCLUSION: In this small cohort, predominantly comprising patients treated with combined meniscal root repair and ACL reconstruction, Lysholm scores improved over 2 years. Within the limited observed extrusion range of 1.20-3.15 mm, no statistically significant association with clinical outcomes was demonstrated. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: IV.

title: Penerapan Metode Fuzzy Time Series Dalam Memprediksi Jumlah Peserta Didik Baru
abstractText: Perencanaan penerimaan peserta didik baru merupakan aspek kritis dalam manajemen pendidikan karena berpengaruh langsung terhadap alokasi sumber daya, kualitas layanan, dan keberlanjutan institusi. Ketidakpastian jumlah pendaftar setiap tahun menjadi tantangan utama bagi pihak sekolah. Penelitian ini bertujuan menerapkan metode Fuzzy Time Series untuk memprediksi jumlah peserta didik baru berdasarkan data historis yang bersifat fluktuatif dan tidak pasti. Metode FTS dipilih karena kemampuannya dalam memodelkan data berbasis linguistik dan mengakomodasi ketidakpastian. Tahapan penelitian meliputi penentuan universe of discourse, pembentukan interval fuzzy, fuzzifikasi, pembentukan Fuzzy Logical Relationship (FLR) dan FLRG, serta defuzzifikasi. Data yang digunakan adalah jumlah peserta didik baru selama lima tahun akademik terakhir. Hasil prediksi dievaluasi menggunakan Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan metode FTS mampu memberikan prediksi yang akurat dengan nilai MAPE sebesar 2.89%, mengindikasikan tingkat kesalahan yang rendah. Simulasi prediksi untuk tahun berikutnya menghasilkan 146 peserta didik. Dengan demikian, penerapan metode FTS dapat menjadi alternatif solusi yang efektif bagi institusi pendidikan dalam mendukung perencanaan strategis penerimaan peserta didik baru berbasis data.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid proteome reveals novel biomarkers for differentiating central NPSLE from central nervous system infection
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Central neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus (cNPSLE) is a major cause of mortality in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Distinguishing cNPSLE from central nervous system (CNS) infections remains a critical clinical challenge due to overlapping clinical manifestations, often leading to diagnostic delays and inappropriate therapeutic interventions. We aimed to identify and validate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers to resolve this diagnostic dilemma. METHODS: We conducted the largest cNPSLE CSF proteomic investigation to date using high-throughput data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS) in a discovery cohort comprising 20 patients with cNPSLE, 8 with CNS infection (cNIC), and 11 non-diseased controls (NDC). Differentially expressed proteins were analyzed for pathway enrichment. Candidate biomarkers were subsequently validated using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in two independent cohorts: an internal validation cohort (46 cNPSLE vs. 29 cNIC) and an external validation cohort (40 cNPSLE vs. 13 cNIC). Robustness of discovery-stage protein selection was assessed by stratified bootstrap resampling and leave-one-out analysis. The diagnostic panel was fitted and locked in the internal cohort, and applied to the external cohort without refitting. RESULTS: Our proteomic profiling quantified 2175 CSF proteins, revealing enrichment in immune and metabolic pathways. We identified three proteins, matrilin-3 (MATN3), tyrosine-protein kinase Mer (MERTK), and V-set and immunoglobulin domain-containing 4 (VSIG4), that were consistently upregulated in cNPSLE compared with both cNIC and NDC groups. In the internal and external validation cohorts, MATN3 demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.875 and 0.868, respectively), followed by MERTK (AUC = 0.801 and 0.775) and VSIG4 (AUC = 0.724 and 0.752). Notably, a composite three-protein panel achieved discriminatory performance, yielding AUCs of 0.921 in the internal cohort and 0.892 in the external cohort, when the locked model trained in the internal cohort was applied without refitting. CONCLUSION: We identified and validated a three-protein CSF panel (MATN3, MERTK, and VSIG4) that differentiates cNPSLE from CNS infections across multi-center cohorts. This diagnostic signature holds potential for clinical translation to facilitate early diagnosis and precise management of NPSLE.

title: Relationship Between Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices and the Incidence of Pediculosis Capitis Among Female Students of State Junior High School 1 Silimakuta
abstractText: Background: Head lice infestation, or pediculosis capitis, remains a significant health challenge in public junior high schools, particularly among adolescent female students. This condition causes high morbidity, potentially leading to a decline in academic performance. Close social interaction, the habit of sharing personal items, and poor personal hygiene are the primary contributing factors. Objective: To determine the relationship between the level of knowledge, attitudes, and practices and the incidence of pediculosis capitis among female students at State Junior High School 1 Silimakuta. Method: This study employed a quantitative design using a cross-sectional approach. The study population consisted of 186 female students from State Junior High School 1 Silimakuta, selected via simple random sampling. Data collection involved self-administered questionnaires followed by physical hair examination. Results: Chi-square test results revealed a highly significant correlation between the level of knowledge and the risk of pediculosis (p = 0.003, RP = 2.465); attitudes also showed a significant association (p = 0.002, RP = 2.680), as did the aspect of practices (p = 0.001, RP = 2.847). Multivariate analysis confirmed that practices were the most dominant predictor of the occurrence of pediculosis capitis. Conclusion: There is a strong relationship between the levels of knowledge, attitudes, and practices and the occurrence of pediculosis capitis among the respondents. Among these three variables, the aspect of practice is the most dominant determining factor.

title: Digital Fraud and Psychological Blackmail Strategies: An Analysis of Scammers' Communications toward the Elderly via Social Media and Instant Messaging Apps
abstractText: Online fraud targeting the elderly is one of the many types of cybercrimes that have emerged as a result of the expansion of digital media, which has also created a large communication area. This study examines the psychological blackmail and communication strategies employed by scammers in fraudulent activities involving phony lottery schemes through Facebook and the instant messaging software WhatsApp. To instill fear, trust, and cooperation in their victims, scammers use images of popular personalities or celebrities, stories of large lottery winnings, and threats of police involvement. This study employs a case study methodology and qualitative techniques, including data from interviews with senior victims and screenshots of online interactions. To find trends in message manipulation, the use of authority symbols, and fear-based persuasion strategies (fear appeals), data analysis is done through communication discourse analysis. The findings reveal that scammers employ a sequential communication strategy consisting of trust building, emotional engagement, authority construction, fear appeal, and psychological blackmail to manipulate older adult victims. These strategies are reinforced through Facebook and WhatsApp interactions, enabling scammers to create perceived legitimacy and urgency. The urgency and credibility of messages are reinforced by digital media. Understanding the communication weaknesses of older adults and the significance of digital literacy techniques in thwarting online fraud are two areas in which this research advances communication science and digital media studies.

title: Quantitative Ethnopharmacological Prioritization of Sundanese Medicinal Plants in Cisarua, West Java
abstractText: Ethnomedicinal knowledge can guide the selection of herbal candidates, but quantitative evidence from West Java is limited. This cross-sectional survey documented medicinal plant use among 31 Sundanese informants in three villages of Cisarua. Semi-structured interviews yielded 224 therapeutic use reports covering 66 taxa from 30 families, from which use-report, citation, fidelity, consensus, family-use, and Jaccard indices were calculated. Knowledge varied widely between informants (median four taxa; range 1–22). Leaves (60.3%), decoction (62.9%), and oral administration (72.8%) predominated. Plantago major L. had the highest use-report count (23), use value (0.742), and relative frequency of citation (0.516), whereas Ageratum conyzoides L. and Musa spp. showed high fidelity for lacerations (80.0% and 81.8%, respectively). Lacerations/cuts formed the largest indication category (39 reports; ICF = 0.789). Taken together, salience, specificity, and report volume identified wound-related taxa as priorities for authentication, standardized extraction, pharmacological validation, and safety assessment.

title: Perancangan dan Implementasi Sistem Informasi Pengelolaan Transaksi dan Persediaan Barang pada Usaha Laundry Berbasis Web
abstractText: Transaction and inventory management in small and medium-sized laundry businesses often still rely on manual, paper-based methods. This leads to slow data retrieval, an increased risk of data loss, and inadequate inventory oversight. Unlike previous studies which primarily focused on managing transactions, customers, services, payments, and financial reporting this research introduces a novel approach by integrating transaction management with inventory (supplies/items) tracking within a single web-based laundry information system. The development process follows the Agile methodology, incorporating data collection through field observations, interviews, and literature reviews, alongside UML modeling. The system is designed for two primary user roles Owner and Cashier with access rights tailored to each. Consequently, since each service type requires specific materials, inventory levels are automatically reduced whenever a transaction is recorded; furthermore, any change in stock can be traced back to the specific transaction that caused it. This streamlines the recording process for cashiers, enables owners to easily monitor the consumption and remaining stock of supplies, and ultimately enhances the quality of customer service. Black Box Testing confirms that all system functions operate as intended.

title: Immersive Virtual Reality for Zero-Emission Education: Exploring Environmental Literacy and Analytical Skills among Elementary Students
abstractText: This study explores immersive virtual reality media to support environmental literacy and analytical skills among elementary school students within the context of zero-emission education. Employing an exploratory design integrating qualitative analysis, descriptive statistics, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), data were collected through interviews, observations, expert evaluations, written feedback, and questionnaires involving three experts and 100 fifth-grade students across eight elementary schools. The results indicate a media feasibility score of 90.34% and a student response score of 81.99%. Specific ratings were 94.05% for content, 91.07% for pedagogy, and 85.71% for media quality. Performance metrics included 85.38% for analytical skills, 83.11% for environmental literacy, 86.89% for media presentation, and 70.81% for practical application. Student experiences were shaped through contextual exploration, environmental change simulations, decision-making, and visual feedback. The media assisted students in identifying problems, tracing cause-and-effect relationships, determining solutions, and drawing conclusions. The assessment prioritized responsible behavior, causal analysis, and solution determination. Successful implementation requires device orientation, simple navigation, clear instructions, and teacher guidance. The study establishes a concept for decision-based immersive environmental learning that emphasizes student agency, environmental consequence evaluation, and the integration of environmental literacy with analytical skills, providing both a theoretical foundation and practical implementation guidelines for schools.

title: Integrated Laxative Effects of Plantago major Leaf Extract on Intestinal Function and Colonic Histology in Loperamide-Induced Constipated Rats
abstractText: This study evaluated the laxative activity of Plantago major leaf extract in loperamide-induced constipated rats. Thirty male Sprague-Dawley rats received no treatment, loperamide alone, loperamide with bisacodyl, or loperamide with P. major extract at 50, 100, or 200 mg/kg body weight (BW). Loperamide reduced fecal number, weight, and water content, intestinal transit ratio, muscular thickness, goblet cell number, and goblet cell area (p < 0.05). The extract increased fecal number and weight, improved intestinal transit, and partially restored colonic histology; 100 mg/kg BW was the only dose that restored both muscular thickness and goblet cell area. P. major leaf extract therefore has laxative activity and is a candidate natural agent for the management of constipation.

title: ANALISIS BIO-HIDROLOGI UNTUK PENGENDALIAN MUKA AIR TANAH DI LAHAN RAWA KABUPATEN HULU SUNGAI UTARA
abstractText: The wetland areas of Hulu Sungai Utara Regency are predominantly composed of backswamp and floodplain ecosystems that function under natural drainage without mechanical control structures. Uncontrolled drainage management risks depressing the shallow groundwater table below the pyritic layer (〖"FeS" 〗_2), which accelerates pyrite oxidation and triggers severe land degradation. This study aims to evaluate the interrelationships among groundwater table depth, pyritic layer depth, redox potential (E_h), soil acidity (pH), and electrical conductivity (EC) to formulate open-channel water management in North Amuntai and South Amuntai Districts. Field surveys and laboratory assessments were performed across 12 representative sampling points using the Hydrological Assessment Framework for Swamp Irrigation Management (HAFSIM). The findings reveal that the pyritic horizon is situated at depths of 40–100 cm, groundwater table depths fluctuate between 15–55 cm, soil E_h values range from +110 to +340 mV, pH levels vary from 4.5 to 5.8, and EC values remain within 0.08–0.18 mS/cm, confirming a non-saline freshwater regime. Weighted evaluations produced a composite score of 0.78 categorized as Undamaged, supporting civil-engineering recommendations to restrict drainage excavation depths above the pyrite layer and construct passive check structures (tabat) to sustain water levels during dry transitions. ABSTRAK Kawasan lahan rawa di Kabupaten Hulu Sungai Utara didominasi oleh ekosistem rawa lebak dan dataran banjir (floodplain) yang mengandalkan sistem drainase alami tanpa pintu air pengatur mekanis. Pengelolaan tata air yang tidak berbasis pada data hidro-kimia berisiko menurunkan muka air tanah (MAT) dangkal di bawah elevasi lapisan pirit (〖"FeS" 〗_2), sehingga memicu terjadinya oksidasi pirit dan degradasi produktivitas lahan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis keterkaitan kedalaman MAT, lapisan pirit, potensial redoks (E_h), derajat keasaman (pH), dan daya hantar listrik (DHL) sebagai dasar penataan sistem tata air saluran terbuka di Kecamatan Amuntai Utara dan Amuntai Selatan. Pengujian dilakukan melalui survei lapangan dan analisis laboratorium pada 12 titik sampel representatif dengan menerapkan kerangka kerja Hydrological Assessment Framework for Swamp Irrigation Management (HAFSIM). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan lapisan pirit berada pada kedalaman 40–100 cm dengan posisi MAT berkisar antara 15–55 cm dari permukaan tanah, nilai E_h berkisar antara +110 mV hingga +340 mV, pH berkisar antara 4,5 hingga 5,8, serta nilai DHL sebesar 0,08–0,18 mS/cm yang mencerminkan tipologi air tawar non-salin. Evaluasi pembobotan menghasilkan skor komposit 0,78 dengan status lahan tergolong Tidak Rusak, sehingga rekomendasi rekayasa tata air difokuskan pada pembatasan kedalaman galian saluran agar tidak memotong pirit serta pemasangan sekat retensi pasif (tabat) pada akhir musim hujan.

title: Penerapan Integrasi mikroRNA dengan Eksosomal Royal Jelly sebagai Terapi untuk Memicu Proses Apoptosis pada OSCC
abstractText: The potential anticancer properties of royal jelly for oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) therapy are a novel area of research. These properties, acting as antioxidants and inhibit tumor growth and induce apoptosis in cancer cells. As the role of microRNAs in cancer biological processes, particularly in OSCC carcinogenesis, has gained importance, the potential synergy between royal jelly and microRNA in cancer therapy is an exciting but underexplored area. Our review comprehensively searched for articles of interest based on the keywords using the snowball method and medical subject heading (MeSH) technique through search engine databases. Royal jelly-combined bioactive compounds are conceptualized to be delivered within extracellular vesicles with microRNA integration. This subsequently targets the OSCC cancer cell, inducing an apoptosis mechanism. Royal jelly exerts an important function in cell metabolism; and this review is potentially exclusively describing possibility for the binding mechanism of royal jelly active compounds with the B-cell lymphoma (Bcl-2) protein and caspase-3 as a target. The delivery system associated with specific microRNAs, such as miR-9, will target the oncogenes of OSCC for tumor growth inhibition. This review will significantly improve the perspective on the royal jelly potencies with modified exosomal delivery and microRNA for OSCC therapy.

title: Determinants of Behavior of Not Consuming Blood Supplement Tablets in Adolescent Women in Jambi City
abstractText: Blood Supplement Tablets (TTD) are one of the efforts to prevent anemia in adolescent girls. TTD consumption compliance can be affected by a variety of factors, including the support of teachers, family, and peers. Objective: This study aims to determine the relationship between teacher support, family support, and peer support with TTD consumption compliance in adolescent girls in Jambi City in 2026.Methods: This study used a cross-sectional design with a quantitative approach. A sample of 100 young women was selected using proportionate stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Data analysis was carried out univariate and bivariate using the Chi-Square test, with a significance level of α=0.05. The magnitude of the relationship was presented using the Prevalence Ratio (PR) and 95% CI.Results: As many as 65.0% of respondents did not comply with the consumption of TTD. Teacher support was not good at 57.0%, family support was not good at 56.0%, and peer support was not good at 53.0%. There was a significant relationship between teacher support and TTD consumption compliance (p=0.001; PR=1.83; 95% CI: 1.28–2.62), family support (p=0.018; PR=1.43; 95% CI: 1.04–1.98), and peer support (p=0.020; PR=1.42; 95% CI: 1.04–1.93).Conclusion: Teacher, family, and peer support was significantly related to TTD consumption compliance in adolescent girls in Jambi City. Strengthening social support through schools, families, and peer groups is needed to increase TTD consumption compliance.

Enhancing Elementary Students' Science Process Skills through Game-Based Learning in Science Education
abstractText: Science process skills (SPS) are essential for elementary students because they enable active engagement in scientific practices such as observing, questioning, predicting, experimenting, collecting data, interpreting data, and concluding. However, science instruction still offers limited opportunities for students to engage directly in these scientific activities, tending to emphasize conceptual understanding over process. This study analyzed the effect of board game-assisted Game-Based Learning on elementary students' SPS in energy-transformation content and identified how these skills developed following the intervention. A quantitative, quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design was used with 52 fourth-grade students: 24 in the experimental group and 28 in the control group. SPS were measured using a performance assessment covering seven indicators. Data were analyzed using normality and homogeneity tests followed by an Independent Sample t-Test. The experimental group's mean score increased from 66.88 to 84.17, while the control group increased from 65.18 to 77.68; the Independent Sample t-Test indicated a significant difference between groups after the intervention (t(50) = -3.593, p < .001), with a large effect size (Cohen's d ≈ 1.00). These findings suggest that board game-assisted Game-Based Learning (JoyR1D3) is a promising interactive alternative for developing elementary students' SPS.

title: IMPLEMENTASI MODEL PEMBELAJARAN MAKE A MATCH DALAM MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA KELAS II SD
abstractText: Low learning outcomes in Pancasila Education among second-grade students at UPTD SD Negeri 076674 Orahili Tanoseo indicated the need for a more active and engaging learning process. This study aimed to describe the implementation of the Make a Match learning model and the improvement of students’ learning outcomes on the topic “I Care for the Environment.” The study employed Classroom Action Research based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model and was conducted in two cycles. The participants were 14 second-grade students, consisting of 6 boys and 8 girls. Data were collected through observations of teacher and student activities, learning achievement tests, and field notes. The data were analyzed using qualitative and quantitative descriptive techniques. The results showed an increase in teacher activity from 51% in the first meeting of Cycle I to 92% in the second meeting of Cycle II. Student activity increased from 58% to 95% across the same meetings. Learning outcomes also improved: the mean score in Cycle I was 67.7, with 36% mastery or 5 of 14 students, while Cycle II reached a mean score of 81.6, with 85% mastery or 12 students. The classical mastery therefore exceeded the predetermined success indicator of 75%. Thus, the Make a Match learning model can be used as an alternative approach to increase student engagement and learning outcomes in Pancasila Education at the elementary school level.

title: Holistic Community Service at Lembaga Kesejahteraan Sosial Anak Widya Asih Blimbingsari: Spiritual Empowerment and Social Support by STT Bethel Indonesia Doctoral Program
abstractText: This community service program aimed to provide holistic support—encompassing spiritual enrichment, educational assistance, and essential daily necessities—to children at Lembaga Kesejahteraan Sosial Anak (LKSA) Widya Asih Blimbingsari, Kecamatan Melaya, Kabupaten Jembrana, Bali. The program was jointly implemented by doctoral students and lecturers from Sekolah Tinggi Teologi Bethel Indonesia (STT Bethel Indonesia), Petamburan Jakarta, coinciding with the institution's commemoration of its 50th Golden Anniversary. A participatory approach was employed, integrating direct service delivery with academic inquiry through interviews with LKSA management and community figures. Core activities included a joint worship service, a devotional sermon, and the distribution of educational materials (notebooks, pens), personal hygiene items (bathing soap, shampoo), and institutional-branded t-shirts to all children. The results demonstrate that the program successfully strengthened the spiritual well-being and academic motivation of the children, provided meaningful material support, and fostered enduring relational bonds between STT Bethel Indonesia and the Christian social welfare institution. The participatory and holistic model employed in this program highlights the pivotal role that theological higher education institutions can play as partners in community-based social welfare, contributing meaningfully to the comprehensive development of children in institutional care.

title: Atomic-scale defect-mediated electronic modulation in monolayer Cu2Pb on Cu(111)
abstractText: Defects are not merely structural imperfections but can serve as atomic-scale regulators of electronic properties in low-dimensional materials. However, how defect-mediated electronic modulation emerges in metallic two-dimensional surface alloys remains largely unexplored. Here, using low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy combined with first-principles calculations, we establish an atomic-scale picture of intrinsic defects in a Cu2Pb monolayer grown on Cu(111), a metallic surface alloy predicted to host nodal-line semimetal states. STM measurements reveal an atomically ordered √3 × √3 surface-alloy structure, providing a well-defined platform for resolving intrinsic defects and their local consequences. We identify intrinsic one-dimensional mirror twin boundaries and multiple point defects, determine their atomic configurations and formation mechanisms, and elucidate their relative energetics. Spectroscopy measurements and electronic-structure calculations reveal localized electronic modulation at mirror twin boundaries, while point defects are characterized in terms of their atomic configurations and formation energetics. These results provide an atomic-scale understanding of intrinsic defects in metallic two-dimensional surface alloys and offer microscopic insight into defect-dependent electronic properties in low-dimensional quantum materials.

title: GAMBARAN SELF-EFFICACY PADA PESERTA DIDIK SLOW LEARNER DI SEKOLAH PENYELENGGARA PENDIDIKAN INKLUSIF
abstractText: Slow learner students face distinctive academic challenges requiring extended processing time, instructional repetition, and individualized learning accommodations. These cognitive dynamics are closely related to the development of self-efficacy, specifically students' confidence in their capabilities to accomplish educational demands. This study aims to describe the self-efficacy of slow learner students in an inclusive junior high school based on three dimensions and four primary sources. A qualitative case study design was employed involving two slow learner students in Surabaya identified through official psychological assessments, alongside a school guidance and counseling teacher as a secondary informant. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews supported by corroborative academic progress reports from the school counselor, followed by interactive data condensation and cross-case analysis. The findings reveal that students' self-efficacy is contextually reflected in task difficulty levels, persistence strength, and subject-matter generality. Furthermore, self-efficacy construction is closely linked to incremental mastery experiences, divergent interpretations of peer performance, perceived meaningfulness of verbal praise, and affective states such as nervousness and embarrassment. ABSTRAK Peserta didik slow learner menghadapi tantangan belajar unik yang menuntut waktu penyerapan materi lebih panjang, repetisi instruksional, serta akomodasi pembelajaran individual. Dinamika kognitif tersebut berkaitan erat dengan pembentukan self-efficacy atau keyakinan peserta didik terhadap kapasitas dirinya dalam menuntaskan tuntutan akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan self-efficacy peserta didik slow learner di sekolah penyelenggara pendidikan inklusif berdasarkan tiga dimensi dan empat sumber pembentuknya. Pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus melibatkan dua peserta didik slow learner jenjang SMP di Kota Surabaya yang diidentifikasi melalui asesmen psikologis resmi, serta satu guru bimbingan dan konseling (BK) sebagai informan sekunder. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur mendalam yang didukung oleh verifikasi laporan perkembangan belajar siswa dari guru BK, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan kondensasi data dan analisis lintas kasus. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa keyakinan diri kedua subjek tercermin secara kontekstual pada tingkat kesulitan tugas (level), daya tahan usaha (strength), dan keberagaman mata pelajaran (generality). Selain itu, pembentukan keyakinan tersebut berkaitan dengan pengalaman keberhasilan bertahap, interpretasi terhadap capaian teman sebaya, kebermaknaan pujian guru, serta kecemasan afektif seperti rasa malu dan gugup.

title: Reorientasi Pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam di Era Digital: Membangun Etika Media Sosial Sejak Pendidikan Dasar
abstractText: Perkembangan teknologi digital menghadirkan tantangan baru bagi pembentukan etika dan karakter murid sekolah dasar, terutama dalam komunikasi daring, penyebaran informasi yang belum terverifikasi, perlindungan privasi, dan respons terhadap perundungan siber. Kondisi ini menunjukkan adanya kesenjangan antara pemahaman nilai-nilai moral dalam pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) dan penerapannya dalam kehidupan digital sehari-hari. Penelitian ini bertujuan merumuskan kerangka konseptual reorientasi pembelajaran PAI yang mengintegrasikan nilai-nilai keislaman dengan pengembangan etika bermedia sosial pada murid sekolah dasar. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode studi kepustakaan (library research). Data diperoleh dari lima buku dan 34 artikel jurnal yang diterbitkan pada 2021–2026, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan metode sintesis tematik melalui tahapan pengodean teks, pengembangan tema deskriptif, dan perumusan tema analitis. Hasil kajian menghasilkan empat dimensi reorientasi pembelajaran PAI, yaitu reorientasi tujuan, konten, metode, dan ekosistem pembelajaran. Reorientasi tujuan menekankan aktualisasi akhlak dalam interaksi digital; reorientasi konten mengintegrasikan nilai tabayyun, kejujuran, amanah, tanggung jawab, kesantunan, dan penghormatan terhadap privasi; reorientasi metode mengutamakan keteladanan, studi kasus, diskusi, refleksi, dan pembiasaan; sedangkan reorientasi ekosistem menekankan kolaborasi antara guru, sekolah, dan orang tua. Kerangka ini menempatkan etika digital sebagai bagian integral dari pengamalan nilai-nilai Islam, bukan sekadar keterampilan menggunakan teknologi. Penelitian ini berkontribusi pada pengembangan landasan konseptual pembelajaran PAI yang kontekstual dan adaptif terhadap perkembangan teknologi. Namun, kerangka tersebut masih bersifat konseptual sehingga memerlukan pengujian empiris untuk mengetahui keterlaksanaan dan efektivitasnya dalam membentuk perilaku digital murid sekolah dasar.

title: Knockdown of the long isoform of the prolactin receptor selectively targets pathogenic immune cells in systemic lupus erythematosus and averts glomerular pathology
abstractText: Abstract Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by chronic inflammation in multiple organ systems. Although elevated circulating levels of the hormone/cytokine prolactin (PRL) have long been associated with increased SLE activity, the extent to which different isoforms of the prolactin receptor (PRLR) contribute to disease pathogenesis has not been explored. Here, we show that immune cells in SLE have aberrant splicing of the PRLR such that the ratio of the long (LF) to short (SF) splice isoforms is increased. To determine whether change in PRLR isoform expression was causal in this disease, we used a splice-modulating oligomer that knocks down expression of the LFPRLR while increasing expression of the SFPRLRs. Using patient samples ex vivo, SLE-prone mice in vivo, high-dimensional flow cytometry, and single-cell RNA sequencing, we demonstrated that the aberrant PRLR isoform expression in SLE both directly and indirectly contributes to the generation of autoreactive immune cell phenotypes. Accordingly, LFPRLR knockdown (KD) reduced STAT1 phosphorylation, decreased expression of type I interferon signaling/response genes known to be biomarkers and hub genes for SLE, reduced immunoglobulins with autoreactivity-associated sequence features, and averted glomerular pathology in SLE-prone mice. Importantly, LFPRLR KD reduced pathogenic B cell and other immune subsets that drive B cell activation, without negative impact on healthy donor counterparts. Current treatments for SLE adversely affect healthy cells and do not concurrently eradicate multiple pathogenic immune subsets. As LFPRLR splice-modulating oligomer does not share these disadvantages, KD of the LFPRLR represents a potential treatment strategy for SLE that merits further investigation.

title: Implementasi Optical Character Recognition dan Algoritma Pencocokan pada Validasi Dokumen Penyumpahan Advokat
abstractText: The documents required for the swearing-in of advocates at Pengadilan Tinggi Padang are still checked manually, making the process time-consuming and prone to recording errors. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a document validation module that integrates Tesseract-based optical character recognition (OCR) with matching algorithms appropriate to each type of data element. The system was developed using the waterfall model as a Laravel-based web application connected to a Python-based OCR microservice and equipped with seven image preprocessing variants. Matching was performed using the Levenshtein distance algorithm for free-text elements and exact matching for elements with standardized formats. Testing involved 74 samples from 10 document types, covering 101 data elements. The test results showed that the overall extraction accuracy reached 89.1%, with the lowest accuracy recorded for Kartu Tanda Penduduk (KTP) documents, at 66.7%. At the matching stage, both algorithms achieved precision, recall, and accuracy values of 100% each. The discrepancies identified in seven data elements resulted from extraction errors rather than the matching logic. These findings indicate that OCR extraction quality is an important aspect of supporting accurate document validation. The developed module serves as a tool to assist in screening the documents required for the swearing-in of advocates, while administrative decisions remain within the authority of legal registry staff.

title: Radial magnetic field component plays a key role in determining the plasma density peak location in magnetized capacitively coupled plasmas
abstractText: Radial plasma uniformity in capacitively coupled plasmas (CCPs) is critical for minimizing variations across the wafer in semiconductor plasma processing. Although magnetic fields have been used to modify plasma profiles, the roles of individual magnetic field components in shaping these profiles remain unclear. Here, magnetic-field-induced plasma profile modification in an argon CCP is investigated using computed tomographic optical emission spectroscopy (CT-OES) and Langmuir probe measurements. In CT-OES, line-integrated optical emission signals acquired from multiple viewing directions are reconstructed into a two-dimensional emissivity distribution, enabling rapid and non-intrusive visualization of the plasma profile. The spatial trends in the reconstructed emissivity distributions are validated by comparison with Langmuir probe measurements. Two single-coil configurations are used to generate distinct radial magnetic field component (Br) distributions. Without an applied magnetic field, the plasma density peak is located near the electrode center. When the magnetic field is applied, the plasma enhancement shifts toward the radial position of maximum Br in both configurations and remains near this position as the coil current is further increased. An opposing-current dual-coil condition displaces the Br maximum without relocating the coils, and the ion density profile forms a broad maximum near the displaced Br maximum rather than near the maxima of the total magnetic flux density (B) or axial magnetic field component (Bz). These results identify the radial position of maximum Br as a practical design parameter for controlling the plasma density peak location in magnetized CCPs.

title: A Stochastic Age-Structured SI Epidemics Model with Logarithmic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Process
abstractText: In this paper, a new stochastic age-structured SI epidemic model with logarithmic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process is proposed. The study mainly focuses on the long-term behavior of solutions for the proposed stochastic system. For this, the existence and (global) asymptotic stability of the equilibria of the deterministic system without OU process are first discussed. Then the properties of extinction and asymptotic persistence of solutions for the stochastic system are investigated and the corresponding threshold conditions for them are obtained successfully. This research highlights the importance of considering randomness in the transmission of the epidemic, especially with complex disease mechanisms and random environmental factors. The findings here reveal that interestingly the reversion speed of the OU process impacts how quickly the system stabilizes, while the magnitude of random disturbances can alter the stability potentially and even cause a resurgence of an infectious disease which is expected to go extinct.

title: Carbon Footprint Estimation of a Higher Education Institution as a Baseline for Sustainable Technological Management: The FIMAZ-UAS Case
abstractText: The carbon footprint has positioned itself as a fundamental tool for the evaluation and management of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in higher education institutions, due to their patterns of energy consumption, resource use, and mobility, which present dynamics comparable to those of small urban areas. In this context, the objective of the present study was to estimate and analyze the institutional carbon footprint of the Faculty of Computer Science Mazatlán (FIMAZ) of the Autonomous University of Sinaloa (UAS), considering the consumption of electricity, drinking water, solid waste generation, and the mobility of students and faculty during the period from January to December 2024. The research was conducted using a quantitative approach, with a non-experimental, descriptive, and longitudinal design, employing a case study based on the guidelines of the GHG Protocol and the ISO 14064-1:2018 standard. The quantification of emissions was carried out using activity data obtained from institutional records and mobility surveys, which were combined with reference emission factors at the national and international levels, allowing for a systematic estimation of the emissions generated by each analyzed source. The results show that electricity consumption is the main source of emissions, with an annual footprint of 220,887.24 kg of CO₂, associated with the intensive use of computing equipment and climate control systems. University mobility constitutes the second largest contribution, with 24,810.15 kg of CO₂, highlighting the private vehicle as the main emitter. The consumption of water and the generation of solid waste contributed 1,422.36 kg of CO₂ and 362.75 kg of CO₂, respectively, related to the intensity of academic activity. These findings allow for the establishment of a technical baseline, the guidance of mitigation strategies, and the strengthening of comprehensive sustainable university environmental management.

title: Smartphones and Parent-Child Interactions: Texting Impacts Behaviors, but No Mere Presence Effect
abstractText: The purpose of this study was to examine changes in parent-child behaviors when the parent was interacting with a smartphone. Technoference or everyday interruptions from smartphone use may lead to lower levels of parent-child engagement. In some cases, the “mere presence” of a smartphone can interfere with interactions, even when the phone is not used. Using a repeated measures design, 30 parent-child dyads (Parents: 26 mothers, 4 fathers, Mage = 33.97 years, SD = 4.93; Children: 16 girls, 14 boys, Mage = 37.14 months, SD = 10.32 months) were videotaped interacting with toys across three conditions including a texting condition, where the parent received and responded to unpredictable text messages, a “mere presence” condition where parents expected to receive text messages, but did not, and a no phone condition where the phone was turned off and out of sight. Videotapes of the dyads were coded for parent and child behaviors across the three conditions. As expected, parents were less responsive, less likely to scaffold their child’s behavior, and engaged in less coordinated joint attention when texting compared to the no phone condition. Children produced more bids for attention when the parents were texting compared to no phone condition. The “mere presence” of a smartphone did not impact the parent or child’s behavior, with responses resembling the no phone condition. These results suggest that actively using a smartphone compromises parent and child behaviors, but the mere presence of the phone does not.

title: Reactive transport modelling of underground structural concrete exposed to aggressive chloride-, sulfate- and carbonate-bearing groundwater
Multiple Distomolar Non-sindromik pada Tiga Kuadran Rahang: Temuan Radiografis dan Pertimbangan Klinis
abstractText: Distomolar is a rare type of supernumerary tooth located distal to the third molar and, being usually asymptomatic, is commonly detected incidentally on panoramic radiographs. This report describes the radiographic findings of nonsyndromic multiple distomolars involving three dental quadrants that were detected incidentally on a panoramic radiograph, and discusses their clinical considerations. A 20-year-old male was referred for panoramic radiography because of intermittent pain in the left mandibular third molar region. The patient had no history of systemic disease or congenital abnormality and showed no clinical features suggestive of a syndrome. The panoramic radiograph revealed three impacted distomolars distal to teeth 18, 28, and 48, impaction of all four third molars, and a diffuse pericoronal radiolucency distal to tooth 38 suggestive of pericoronal inflammation. The findings were explained to the patient, who was referred back to the referring dentist with the radiographic report for definitive diagnosis and treatment planning. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is recommended as a further examination if surgical treatment is planned. Multiple distomolars may be detected incidentally on panoramic radiographs obtained for other complaints. Systematic radiographic interpretation is essential to identify these rare developmental anomalies and to support appropriate clinical decision-making.

title: Bose-Einstein Condensation of a Coherently Coupled Lee-Huang-Yang Gas
Influence of dielectric environment on the optical properties of the CVD-grown monolayer WSe2
abstractText: Regulating excitonic emission in two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors through external perturbations offers an effective route to improving the performance of their optoelectronic devices. Here, we investigate the evolution of exciton and trion emissions in monolayer tungsten diselenide (WSe2) under different dielectric environments using temperature-dependent Raman and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy. Through deconvolution of the PL spectra, it is observed that both low temperature and high-dielectric environment facilitate the formation of trions, leading to an increase in their integrated intensity compared with that of the neutral excitons. This phenomenon can be attributed to the higher trion binding energy at low temperature and the dielectric-induced deep-to-shallow transition of defect levels, which modifies the effective charged defect levels in WSe2 and consequently influences the formation and recombination dynamics of the excitons and trions differently. Our results provide deeper insight into the emission mechanisms of excitonic complexes in 2D semiconductors under dielectric environments and offer useful guidance for dielectric engineering of optoelectronic and photonic devices based on transition metal dichalcogenides.

The Digital Divide in Global Communication: Inequality, Governance, and the Contest for Narrative Power
abstractText: The spread of information and communication technologies has made connectivity central to global communication, yet the benefits of this transformation are distributed unequally. This article examines the digital divide as a structural feature of contemporary global media rather than a mere gap in hardware access. Drawing on scholarship that treats the divide as a complex and dynamic phenomenon, it argues that the divide operates on at least three intersecting levels: access, usage and skill, and algorithmic and infrastructural power. It then traces how the divide is deepened by the politics of platform governance and by asymmetric control over digital content, and considers how these asymmetries become acute in armed conflict, where the ability to generate, moderate, and frame information is itself a weapon. The article concludes that bridging the divide requires not only connectivity and digital literacy but a redistribution of the power to produce and govern the global media environment.

The mediating effects of perceived quality and brand image between country-of-origin and purchase intention for refurbished iPhones
abstractText: This study investigates how Country-of-Origin influences Students’ Purchase Intention toward Refurbished iPhones, with Brand Image and Perceived Quality as mediating variables. A quantitative explanatory design was applied, involving 136 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS). The empirical results revealed that Country-of-Origin positively and significantly affected Brand Image, Perceived Quality, and purchase intention, both directly and indirectly. Brand Image and Perceived Quality were also confirmed to mediate the relationship between Country-of-Origin and purchase intention. These findings underscore the role of Country-of-Origin as a quality signal shaping consumer perceptions and purchase intentions regarding refurbished high-technology products, and contribute to a deeper understanding of consumer behavior while offering insights for marketing strategies in emerging markets.

title: Esperanza y agencia para reinventar la educación hacia futuros justos y habitables
abstractText: Este artículo analiza la forma en la que la educación puede ir más allá de una adaptación tecnocrática a la crisis climática para avanzar hacia una Bildung planetaria basada en la justicia y la agencia democrática. Proponemos un marco de Ecopedagogía Crítica Transformadora (ECT) que se nutre de cuatro fuentes teóricas: la teoría histórico-cultural de Vygotsky, la pedagogía crítica de Freire, el trabajo escolar cooperativo de Freinet y el análisis descolonial de la injusticia epistémica. La ECT organiza la práctica en torno a cuatro ejes —crítico-descolonial, sistémico, afectivo-ético y lugar-dialógico— y tres ritmos conceptuales que van desde la problematización hasta la historización, el análisis mediado y el discurso público. El artículo propone una crítica a los enfoques de “cero emisiones netas” y de competencias que despolitizan el conocimiento; principios fundamentales para diseños que legitimen epistemologías plurales y emociones políticas; y criterios de evaluación que hagan hincapié en la mediación, la utilidad pública y la praxis colectiva. Las implicaciones políticas incluyen la reformulación de las normas en torno a las alfabetizaciones descoloniales, la protección del tiempo dedicado a la pedagogía dialógica y la construcción de una gobernanza que haga realidad la autonomía de los estudiantes. La ECT ofrece un marco operativo para reorientar la educación hacia futuros plurales, justos y habitables.

Classification of Flood-Prone Areas in Padang City Using Landsat-9 Satellite Imagery
abstractText: Flood-susceptibility mapping requires spatial information that captures the combined influence of hydrological conditions, topography, soils, and land cover. This study classified and mapped flood-prone areas in Padang City by integrating six parameters: rainfall, elevation, slope, distance from rivers, soil type, and land use/land cover. A quantitative spatial approach using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) was employed. Land cover was classified from Landsat-9 Collection 2 Level-2 imagery using the Classification and Regression Trees (CART) algorithm in Google Earth Engine. The six parameters were subsequently scored, weighted, and integrated through weighted-overlay analysis. The land-cover classification achieved an overall accuracy of 85.17%, while the overlay analysis delineated five flood-susceptibility classes. Moderate susceptibility occupied the largest area, covering 30,675.414 ha (45.79%), followed by high susceptibility at 17,631.140 ha (26.32%), low susceptibility at 17,226.524 ha (25.72%), very high susceptibility at 1,420.275 ha (2.12%), and very low susceptibility at 31.048 ha (0.05%). These findings reveal substantial spatial variation in flood susceptibility across Padang City, with moderate susceptibility predominating. The study provides an integrated spatial assessment to support disaster mitigation and environmentally responsive land-use planning.

title: A A Comparative Study of Multimodal Discourse in Micro-Learning Videos via Intersemiotic Complementarity Theory
abstractText: With the increasing popularity of online educational videos, how to teach and disseminate these videos has become a challenge for many creators. But few of the current studies discussed the intersemiotic complementarity of micro-learning videos and how to promote their effectiveness through this angle. Based on the intersemiotic complementarity theory, this research explores how the collaborative interaction between micro-learning videos’ image and text affects the effectiveness of teaching and dissemination. This study compares and analyzes the image-text relationship of the two videos, Crash Course (CC) and Home Revise (HR) from ideational, interpersonal and compositional intersemiotic complementarity (IC). The study finds that: (1) For ideational IC, both videos use synonymy, collocation and hyponymy, and repetition is often combined with other relationship types to form a composite type. (2) For interpersonal IC, CC uses a lot of demand shots, and the text mood is diverse, so as to build a sense of interaction. (3) For compositional IC, the layout of CC is more flexible. In contrast, the layout of HR is relatively fixed and monotonous. The results of this study show that good ideational IC can reduce the cognitive burden and promote the teaching effectiveness; highly interactive interpersonal IC can improve audience participation; good compositional IC can balance teaching and fun. This study expands the application of intersemiotic complementarity in video analysis, and also provides inspirations for the design and evaluation of micro-learning videos.

title: Predicting water vapor egress rate through elastomeric needle shields of prefilled syringes
abstractText: Abstract Prefilled syringes (PFSs) with staked-in-needles are widely used for high-concentration biologics but are vulnerable to needle clogging driven by water evaporation of trapped liquid in the needle lumen. This study quantitatively links trapped liquid volume, water vapor egress, and drying dynamics to inform device- and condition-dependent clogging risk. Commercial staked-in-needle PFSs with three rigid needle shield (RNS) elastomer formulations were characterized by X-ray computed tomography (XRCT). Elastomer water vapor permeabilities measured under controlled temperature and humidity were utilized. These data parameterized a steady-state Fickian diffusion model in COMSOL Multiphysics ® to compute water vapor concentration fields and water egress rates as functions of temperature, relative humidity, and needle/RNS design. A closed-form expression for egress rate and a Pareto sensitivity analysis were derived. Simulations showed water egress rates ranged from 0 to 0.7 nL/day, increasing with temperature and elastomer permeability and decreasing with ambient humidity, accompanied by minor influence of needle geometry within the tested range of 0.275 and 0.300 mm inner diameter and needle insertion depth shifts (± 1 mm). Estimated evaporation times for 4.5–13.3 nL liquid droplets can span days to months depending on storage conditions. This integrated experimental–computational framework quantitatively relates nanoliter-scale liquid retention to vapor-driven drying in staked-in-needle PFSs and identifies temperature, humidity, and elastomer permeability as key levers to mitigate needle-clogging risk at the device level.

title: Unsaturated fatty acid metabolism and FADS2 as candidate factors in triple-negative breast cancer
abstractText: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is aggressive and lacks effective targeted therapies. Using estrogen receptor (ER)-negative breast cancer as a proxy for TNBC, we explored circulating metabolite associations and downstream candidate genes. A two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis used large-scale metabolome genome-wide association study data (~1,400 metabolites). Candidate metabolites underwent Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment. Computationally predicted targets were intersected with common differentially expressed genes from three Gene Expression Omnibus datasets and Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis modules. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator-Cox and random survival forest prioritized genes in the Cancer Genome Atlas–TNBC. Single-cell RNA-seq (GSE176078) explored heterogeneity and pathways. MR identified 38 candidate metabolites nominally associated with ER-negative breast cancer risk, enriched in unsaturated fatty acid and arachidonic acid metabolism. Integration yielded 39 candidate genes, and survival-based machine learning prioritized KRAS, MGST3, FADS2, UGT8, IDO1, and SRC. Single-cell analysis showed higher FADS2 in a presumed malignant epithelial subpopulation (log2FC = 2.53, false discovery rate < 0.05), associated with cholesterol biosynthesis, sterol metabolism, and cell-cycle programs. These exploratory findings nominate abnormal circulating unsaturated fatty acid metabolism and FADS2 as candidate factors in ER-negative/TNBC biology. FADS2 is a candidate biomarker and potential target requiring TNBC-specific genetic, patient-aware single-cell, prognostic, and experimental validation.

title: GELAS EMOSI DAN GELAS HARAPAN: PSIKOEDUKASI BERBASIS EXPRESSIVE WRITING UNTUK MENDUKUNG RESILIENSI SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui perubahan tingkat resiliensi siswa kelas VI SDN 01 Ciherang setelah mengikuti program psikoedukasi Gelas Emosi dan Gelas Harapan berbasis expressive writing. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain one-group pre-test and post-test diterapkan kepada 42 siswa kelas VI yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan instrumen adaptasi Child and Youth Resilience Measure-Revised (CYRM-R) yang mencakup dimensi personal dan caregiver. Data yang terkumpul dianalisis menggunakan teknik statistik deskriptif, uji normalitas Shapiro-Wilk, serta uji komparatif non-parametrik Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rerata skor total resiliensi siswa mengalami kenaikan kecil dari 44,7 (SD = 4,12) pada saat pre-test menjadi 44,8 (SD = 3,98) pada saat post-test. Akan tetapi, hasil uji hipotesis membuktikan bahwa peningkatan skor tersebut tidak berbeda secara signifikan secara statistik (Z = -0,889, p = 0,374). Hasil yang tidak signifikan juga teridentifikasi pada dimensi personal (p = 0,692) maupun dimensi caregiver (p = 0,471). Ketiadaan perubahan yang signifikan tersebut dipengaruhi oleh tingginya skor dasar resiliensi siswa sebelum intervensi (ceiling effect) serta rentang waktu pelaksanaan kegiatan yang tergolong singkat. Kendati demikian, kegiatan expressive writing memberikan ruang katarsis yang aman bagi peserta didik untuk mengenali, mengekspresikan, dan merefleksikan pengalaman emosionalnya secara adaptif. Program intervensi lanjutan disarankan untuk menambah durasi sesi intervensi serta mengintegrasikan peran guru dan orang tua dalam mendampingi perkembangan psikologis anak. ABSTRACT This study aimed to examine changes in the resilience levels of sixth-grade students at SDN 01 Ciherang after participating in the Gelas Emosi dan Gelas Harapan psychoeducational program based on expressive writing. A quantitative method with a one-group pre-test and post-test design was employed involving 42 sixth-grade students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using the Indonesian adaptation of the Child and Youth Resilience Measure-Revised (CYRM-R), which encompasses both personal and caregiver dimensions. The acquired data were subsequently analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro-Wilk normality test, and the non-parametric Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The findings revealed that the mean total resilience score increased slightly from 44.7 (SD = 4.12) at the pre-test to 44.8 (SD = 3.98) at the post-test. However, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test indicated that this difference was not statistically significant (Z = -0.889, p = 0.374). Similar non-significant outcomes were observed across both the personal dimension (p = 0.692) and the caregiver dimension (p = 0.471). This lack of statistical significance was primarily attributable to a high baseline score prior to intervention, which produced a ceiling effect, as well as the relatively brief intervention timeframe. Nevertheless, the expressive writing process offered students a safe and structured reflective medium to recognize, articulate, and process their emotional experiences constructively. Future interventions are recommended to implement prolonged, multi-session activities while actively involving parents and classroom teachers to achieve optimal psychological adaptation.

title: Literacy Promotion and Child Health: The Role of Reach Out and Read
abstractText: This Special Article draws on a State of the Art Plenary, Literacy Promotion and Child Health: Reach Out and Read at 37, presented at the 2026 Pediatric Academic Societies meeting, which reviewed the evolution of Reach Out and Read (ROR) as a clinical intervention, a subject of research, and an increasingly incorporated component of pediatric primary care. The ROR model, supported by a national organization, now reaches 4.8 million children and families throughout the United States. Much of this growth has been driven by clinicians seeking to support family relationships, child development, and educational trajectories through primary care, especially for families at social risk. This article is based on 6 brief talks, each identified by theme and speaker, focusing on the original concept and rationale for early literacy promotion in pediatric primary care; ROR as an instrument for social justice in the context of brain development, toxic stress, and resilience; efforts to define critical elements of the intervention and strengthen them through training and engagement of both practicing clinicians and residents; a multistage collaborative research effort centering parent leaders across the ROR network in the design of the CONNECT Survey, a measure of the parent/caregiver-clinician relationship; and the crucial contribution of parent voice. Research on ROR has shown positive effects on parent reading and child vocabulary; more recent research, highlighting parent/caregiver voices, emphasizes the importance of modeling by clinicians and of the relationships between primary care clinicians and families.

title: Technology-Enhanced Hybrid Service-Learning in Higher Education: Insights from a Bibliometric Study
abstractText: Technology-Enhanced Hybrid Service-Learning (HSL) has emerged as an innovative pedagogical approach that integrates experiential community engagement with digitally mediated learning environments in higher education. Despite its growing implementation, scholarly knowledge on the intellectual structure, development trajectory, and thematic evolution of HSL remains fragmented. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of HSL research in higher education, drawing on 154 peer-reviewed journal articles indexed in the Scopus database between 2010 and 2026. Using PRISMA-guided screening procedures and bibliometric tools including biblioMagika®, VOSviewer, and OpenRefine, the study analyses publication trends, citation patterns, influential contributors, leading institutions and countries, source titles, highly cited documents, and keyword co-occurrence networks. The findings reveal a marked acceleration in research output from 2010 onwards, coinciding with the global expansion of hybrid and online learning models. While early publications were limited in number, they demonstrated high citation impact, forming a strong conceptual foundation for subsequent scholarship. The United States leads in publication volume, whereas Malaysia and Hong Kong demonstrate particularly strong citation performance relative to output. Prominent source titles reflect the interdisciplinary nature of HSL, spanning educational technology, sustainability, and experiential learning domains. Keyword co-occurrence analysis highlights “service learning,” “higher education,” and “student engagement” as central themes, alongside growing emphasis on online learning and e-service learning modalities. Overall, the study demonstrates that Technology-Enhanced Hybrid Service-Learning represents a dynamic and increasingly mature research domain characterised by global participation, collaborative authorship, and evolving thematic integration of pedagogy and technology. By systematically mapping the field’s intellectual structure and scholarly influence, this study provides an updated foundation for future research, pedagogical innovation, and policy development in higher education.

title: Advances in therapeutic oligonucleotide conjugates
abstractText: Abstract Oligonucleotide therapeutics (ONTs) have revolutionized the medical landscape by enabling the precise modulation of genetic pathways. This perspective highlights the major conjugation strategies for ONTs, using antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) and small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) as representative modalities. We describe diverse classes of targeting ligands, including small molecules, cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs), antibodies, and aptamers. For example, triantennary N -acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) conjugation has enabled a number of approved oligonucleotide therapeutics. Meanwhile, other emerging conjugation technologies have expanded oligonucleotide delivery to extrahepatic tissues to address a broader range of diseases. We further summarize the clinical translation of these delivery platforms, highlighting approved therapeutics alongside emerging clinical candidates. Finally, we provide an outlook on challenges and opportunities for the next generation of oligonucleotide therapeutics.

title: Webinar-Based Capacity Building for Integrated STEM: Pre-Service Teachers' Engineering Design Process (EDP) Oriented Lessons
abstractText: The Philippine Department of Education emphasizes the engineering design process (EDP) as a pedagogical approach for developing problem solvers and innovators, yet Filipino learners remain among the lowest performers in science internationally. Engineering design is widely regarded as the central integrator of integrated STEM instruction, yet its integration is hardest in the life sciences, where abstract, submicroscopic phenomena and dependence on technologies unavailable in ordinary classrooms constrain what teachers can design. This study examined a webinar-based capacity building intervention preparing pre-service science teachers to develop EDP-oriented lesson plans and activities for Cell and Molecular Biology. Delivered as a one-month, three-session synchronous webinar series with digital scaffolds such as editable lesson templates, annotated exemplars, and shared resources, the intervention was evaluated using a mixed-method design with 24 third-year pre-service science teachers. Lesson plan evaluations improved from "Moderately Evident" (M = 4.01) to "Highly Evident" (M = 4.68), a statistically significant difference (p < 0.05). EDP-oriented activities were rated "Highly Evident" (M = 4.33) and demonstration teaching "Satisfactory" (M = 87.36). Four themes emerged: Value of EDP in STEM Education, Impact of the Webinar Series, Challenges in Implementing EDP, and Novel Experiences and Insights. Notably, participants' most persistent constraint was technological: access to affordable, accessible materials for rendering cellular processes designable. Findings indicate that technology-mediated capacity building can prepare pre-service teachers for integrated STEM in the life sciences, but that teacher education must also equip them with low-cost tools for visualizing and modelling submicroscopic phenomena.

Interfacial Schottky-barrier-assisted optoelectronic resistive switching and synaptic plasticity in ITO/BiFeO3/ZnO/BiFeO3/Ag heterostructure memristors
abstractText: An ITO/BiFeO3/ZnO/BiFeO3/Ag heterostructure memristor was fabricated by magnetron sputtering and post-annealing to investigate Schottky-barrier-assisted resistive switching and synaptic plasticity. Structural characterization confirms the formation of a compact BiFeO3/ZnO/BiFeO3 multilayer film with nanocrystalline morphology and distinct ZnO and BiFeO3 phases. The device exhibits stable bipolar resistive switching, and illumination enhances the resistance-state separation by modulating carrier concentration and oxygen-vacancy-related defect states. Transport analysis indicates Ohmic conduction at low bias, while Schottky emission dominates the higher-bias region, revealing the important role of BiFeO3/ZnO interfacial barriers. The switching behavior is primarily associated with oxygen-vacancy-assisted conductive pathway formation and rupture, while reversible Schottky barrier modulation at the heterointerfaces further regulates carrier transport. Furthermore, illumination- and pulse-interval-dependent long-term potentiation and depression are demonstrated, revealing optically tunable synaptic plasticity. These results suggest that the BiFeO3/ZnO/BiFeO3 heterostructure provides an effective platform for optoelectronic memristors and artificial synaptic devices.

title: Pensar las micorrizas: Debates filosóficos sobre la mesada
abstractText: 1. Una práctica biológica habitual para el estudio de los hongos del suelo consiste en su aislamiento in vitro. Sin embargo, esta metodología presenta dificultades cuando se trata de hongos formadores de ectomicorrizas (HFE). Sucesivos intentos fallidos mostraron una ventana epistemológica y ontológica que expone los límites de prácticas científicas basadas en la separación y abstracción de lo vivo.2. Este trabajo propone una reflexión interdisciplinaria sobre los supuestos que orientan nuestras prácticas científicas. Para ello, se realizó una revisión historiográfica y filosófica sobre los conceptos de individuo y simbiosis usados a menudo. La revisión fue contrastada con las experiencias de laboratorio propias y de otros investigadores en la temática, recopiladas a partir de una encuesta.3. La revisión nos permitió ver que las problemáticas asociadas a la definición de individuo no son nuevas y que los organismos que participan de la simbiosis se podrían considerar como una totalidad (holobionte) indivisible.4. Las respuestas de especialistas en la temática sugieren que la dificultad de aislar HFE es persistente y podría responder tanto a cuestiones técnicas como al carácter relacional de la simbiosis.5. Implicancias. Las dificultades experimentales poseen valor epistemológico más allá del problema técnico. Esto nos invita a revisar la aplicación de ciertas metodologías cuando se trata con organismos muy interdependientes, así como a pensarlos desde perspectivas relacionales. De esta manera, proponemos reconocer las discusiones interdisciplinarias como guía para nuevas prácticas científicas y epistemológicas, ya que habilitan nuevos horizontes de trabajo y podrían ser la clave hacia nuevas formas de estudio de lo viviente.

Agent-based simulation of shared autonomous electric vehicle fleets: application to Montreal Olympic Park
abstractText: Abstract Many cities now offer shared vehicle fleets as an alternative mode of daily transportation. These fleets can be further enhanced through the use of autonomous or electric autonomous vehicles, which reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, lower staffing requirements, enable automated charging, and provide smoother operation. This paper proposes an agent-based simulation framework to model a fleet of shared electric autonomous vehicles (SEAVs) providing one-way, short-distance trips. A case study is conducted for Montreal’s Olympic Park, encompassing five strategically located stations. By varying key fleet parameters, 105 scenarios are generated and analyzed. Results indicate that a fleet of 20 vehicles with a 50 km range and 30 parking spots can meet demand across all tested customer arrival frequencies, achieving service performance rates of 90% or higher. Vehicle range is shown to have minimal impact on performance compared to fleet size and demand probability. Additionally, reducing the number of parking spots decreases the number of rejected customers but increases the number of empty trips.

Optimization of N, P, and K Fertilizer Rates for ‘IPB 13S’ Rice
abstractText: Fertilizer recommendations for newly released rice varieties need to be optimized because nutrient requirements may vary among varieties and growing environments. ‘IPB 13S’ is a newly released rice variety developed by IPB University, and information regarding its optimal nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P2O5), and potassium (K2O) requirements is still limited. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the optimal rates of N, P2O5, and K2O fertilizers for ‘IPB 13S’ rice. The study was conducted from May to September 2024 at the Sawah Baru Experimental Farm, Dramaga, Bogor, Indonesia. Three fertilizer experiments (N, P2O5, and K2O) were arranged in a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with five fertilizer levels (0%, 50%, 100%, 150%, and 200% of the regional recommended rate) and three replications. Growth parameters, yield components, grain yield, and nutrient use efficiency were evaluated. Data were analyzed using analysis of variance, orthogonal polynomial analysis, and quadratic regression. The results showed that N, P2O5, and K2O applications significantly affected plant growth, yield components, grain yield, and nutrient use efficiency. Quadratic regression analysis identified optimal fertilizer rates of 170 kg N/ha, 53 kg P2O5/ha, and 71 kg K2O/ha, resulting in the highest predicted grain yield. These findings indicate that variety-specific fertilizer recommendations are needed to optimize grain yield and nutrient use efficiency in the ‘IPB 13S’ rice variety.

Smartwatch-based pelvic tracking system for augmented reality navigation in total hip arthroplasty: a preliminary clinical study
abstractText: Abstract Background Accurate assessment of pelvic orientation is essential for acetabular cup placement during total hip arthroplasty (THA). Conventional pelvic tracking systems generally rely on dedicated tracking hardware and optical tracking infrastructure. We developed a smartwatch-based pelvic tracking system integrated with an augmented reality (AR) navigation platform and evaluated its preliminary clinical performance. Methods This retrospective study included 30 hips of 27 consecutive patients who underwent primary THA using a smartwatch-based pelvic tracking navigation system between May 2025 and April 2026. The system utilizes a commercially available smartwatch fixed to the iliac crest as a pelvic tracking device and communicates orientation information to a smartphone-based AR navigation platform via Bluetooth. Acetabular cup orientation was evaluated using postoperative CT. Absolute radiographic inclination (RI) and anteversion (RA) errors were calculated as absolute differences between the final intraoperative navigation measurements and postoperative CT measurements. Results The mean absolute RI error was 2.8° ± 2.1°, and the mean absolute RA error was 3.6° ± 2.2°. Postoperative CT measurements were within 5° of the final intraoperative navigation measurements for RI and RA in 86.7% and 70.0% of hips, respectively. Navigation was successfully completed in all 30 hips, with no conversion to a backup technique. Additional bench testing demonstrated reproducible smartwatch reattachment and reduction of time-dependent relative orientation differences following FPP invocation. Conclusions This study demonstrated the feasibility of integrating a commercially available smartwatch into a pelvic tracking system for THA navigation. The smartwatch-based pelvic tracking platform achieved a preliminary range of cup-positioning accuracy without requiring continuous optical visualization of a pelvic reference marker while utilizing a compact and widely available consumer wearable device. This study represents the first step toward wearable-device-based navigation in arthroplasty.

Hybrid Intelligence as a Tool for Textual Decoding: Integrating the Literary Detective Framework in Higher Education
abstractText: This paper explores the transformative integration of Hybrid Intelligence (HI) within the landscape of higher philological education, specifically operationalized through the innovative 'Literary Detective' pedagogical framework. Amidst the shifting cognitive baselines of the digital era, this study addresses the crisis of sustained deep attention by proposing a synergistic model of textual archaeology. The research focuses on the intricate process of multidimensional decoding, wherein human cultural intuition collaborates with the computational power of Large Language Models (LLMs) to excavate latent intertextual layers across a diverse literary corpus.The study provides a comparative analysis of foundational and modern texts, demonstrating how a structured Decoding Matrix facilitates the identification of complex cultural codes in the cosmological epics of Vaja-Pshavela, the impressionistic prose of Niko Lortkipanidze, and the tragic war poetry of Mirza Gelovani, alongside the works of Homer, Margaret Atwood, and Ana Kalandadze. The findings reveal that Artificial Intelligence, when utilized as a cognitive scaffold rather than a replacement for authorial voice, significantly amplifies the student's capacity to navigate intertextual networks and resolve “artificial hallucinations” through intuitive filtering. Empirical evidence suggests that this hybrid approach not only increases the efficiency of thematic identification by approximately 38% but also fosters advanced critical thinking and digital literacy. Ultimately, the paper argues for a paradigm shift in the humanities, positioning the student as an active investigator in an AI-augmented hermeneutic environment, ensuring the continued relevance of philological rigor in a post-digital academic world.
