title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Integration in Education: Teachers’ Utilization, Perceptions, and Implementation Challenges
abstractText: This study explored the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in chemistry instruction, focusing on teachers’ utilization patterns, perceptions, and the challenges they encounter. A sample of 18 chemistry teachers from various institutions participated, providing insights into the types and frequency of AI tools used, including ChatGPT, ChemCollective, and PhET Interactive Simulations. Findings indicate that generative AI tools—particularly ChatGPT—are the most widely adopted due to their accessibility, versatility, and ease of integration. In contrast, subject-specific and creative AI platforms remain underutilized, suggesting that familiarity, perceived complexity, and awareness significantly influence adoption patterns. Teachers demonstrated strongly positive perceptions of AI integration in both curriculum and instruction, recognizing its potential to enhance content delivery, student engagement, personalized learning, and the development of 21st-century skills. No significant differences were found across institutions, indicating a shared readiness to integrate AI in chemistry education. Despite these favorable perceptions, effective implementation is constrained by technical limitations, infrastructure gaps, data quality concerns, usability challenges, ethical issues, and privacy risks. Teachers also expressed concerns about over-reliance on AI and the potential reduction of meaningful teacher–student interaction, emphasizing the importance of maintaining a balanced, human-centered approach. Overall, the findings support the strategic and guided adoption of AI as a pedagogical enhancement tool rather than a substitute for professional judgment and instructional expertise. The results highlight the need for structured, discipline-specific professional development that emphasizes prompt literacy, critical evaluation of AI outputs, ethical awareness, and pedagogical alignment. Strengthening technological infrastructure, establishing sustained institutional support systems, and developing clear guidelines for responsible AI use are essential to ensure effective, equitable, and ethically grounded integration of AI in chemistry education.

title: Pengaruh Struktur Modal dan Ukuran Perusahaan terhadap Manajemen Laba pada Perusahaan Properti dan Real Estat di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2019-2023
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh rasio utang jangka panjang, rasio utang jangka pendek, dan ukuran perusahaan terhadap manajemen laba pada perusahaan properti dan real estat yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2019–2023. Sebagai industri padat modal, perusahaan ini sangat bergantung pada pembiayaan eksternal yang berpotensi menimbulkan tekanan finansial, sehingga memicu praktik manajemen laba demi merekayasa kinerja keuangan. Metode penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan analisis deskriptif dan regresi data panel. Data sekunder diperoleh dari laporan keuangan resmi di website Bursa Efek Indonesia (www.idx.co.id). Variabel dependen yaitu manajemen laba diukur dengan Discretionary Accruals (DA), sedangkan variabel independen meliputi rasio utang jangka panjang diukur dengan Long-term Debt Ratio (LtDr), rasio utang jangka pendek diukur dengan Short-term Debt Ratio (StDr), dan ukuran perusahaan diukur dengan logaritma natural Total Aset (Firm Size). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa secara parsial, rasio utang jangka panjang berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap manajemen laba. Sebaliknya, rasio utang jangka pendek berpengaruh negatif dan tidak signifikan, serta ukuran perusahaan berpengaruh positif tetapi tidak signifikan. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa rasio utang jangka panjang merupakan faktor dominan yang mendorong manajer melakukan praktik manajemen laba, sementara utang jangka pendek dan skala ukuran perusahaan tidak memberikan kontribusi yang signifikan dalam memengaruhi keputusan tersebut.

Critical behavior, variable range hopping, and probable topological Hall effect in VCr2Te4 single crystal
abstractText: Chromium tellurides are taken as a board for probing nontrivial spin interactions. Besides changing the Cr/Te ratio or dimension, doping can also tune the physical properties of these compounds. However, only magnetic properties of doped chromium tellurides polycrystalline have been reported, and physical properties of heteroatom-substituting chromium-tellurium single crystals are few. Here, we prepared VCr2Te4 single crystals and studied the electrical transport, magnetic properties, and Hall effect of the single crystals. VCr2Te4 displays perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and a ferrimagnetic-to-paramagnetic transition at ∼74 K. Magnetic critical exponents β = 0.446(2) with TC = 74.512(1) K and γ = 1.081(2) with TC = 74.526(1) K are obtained from the Arrott–Noakes equation of states with long-range interactions between spins that decay as J(r) ≈ r−4.638, indicating intricate magnetic interactions in the VCr2Te4 single crystal. The sample shows a semiconductor-like behavior above 100 K due to variable range hopping. VCr2Te4 has n-type carriers and a larger anomalous Hall conductivity σxy ∼ 104 Ω−1 cm−1 at 3 K. Based on scaling analysis, the anomalous Hall effect mechanism is the skew scattering. A topological Hall effect can be observed up to 20 K due to the noncoplanar spin configuration. Our results reveal the interesting physical properties in VCr2Te4 single crystals and give a way to tune physical properties of chromium tellurides and design the future chromium-telluride-based device.

abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis strategi penetapan harga yang ditetapkan pada bisnis online group order (go) dan respon anggota komunitas di media sosial pada group order komunitas penggemar K-pop, khususnya group order by EL yang fokusnya pada grup Ateez. Peneliti menggunakan jenis penelitian kualitatif dengan pendekatan netnografi. Pengumpulan data dilakukan dengan observasi secara digital pada informasi kegiatan, interaksi, dan komunikasi, serta respon pada media sosial yaitu Line, X, dan e-commerce Shopee. Hasil penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa group order by EL tidak hanya fokus dalam strategi penetapan harga berdasarkan biaya namun juga penilaian anggota berupa nilai kepercayaan. Kegiatan transaksi yang terjadi dalam group order by EL terbukti dilakukan dilengkapi dengan bukti pendukung melibatkan respon anggota dengan kalimat positif dan emoticon yang menunjukkan kepuasan pada ulasan dan komentar dalam media sosial. title: PENGEMBANGAN DAN KELAYAKAN LKPD BERBASIS STEM PADA MATERI EKOSISTEM UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KETERAMPILAN BERPIKIR KRITIS SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR
abstractText: This study aimed to develop and examine the feasibility and practicality of a Student Worksheet (LKPD) based on Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) on Ecosystem topics oriented toward elementary school students' critical thinking skills. The development procedure applied a Research and Development (R&D) method using the ADDIE model encompassing Analyze, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation stages. The research was conducted at MIS Ad-Dakwah Kabanjahe during the even semester of the 2025/2026 academic year, involving 25 fifth-grade students and three classroom teachers. Data collection instruments comprised expert validation rating sheets and user practicality questionnaires. Validation results demonstrated that the product was in the highly feasible category, with scores of 90.59% from subject-matter experts, 90.00% from media design experts, 89.00% from language experts, and 91.00% from test instrument experts. Practicality testing showed a highly practical qualification, reaching 90.00% in individual trials, 94.00% in small-group trials, 92.00% in large-group trials, and 90.00% from teacher responses. Therefore, the STEM-based LKPD on Ecosystems is declared highly feasible and practical for facilitating critical thinking activities in elementary science education.

title: Antibacterial Activity of Eugenia uniflora L. Leaf Extract Against Staphylococcus epidermidis: An In Vitro and In Silico Study
abstractText: Acne is an inflammatory skin disorder commonly associated with Staphylococcus epidermidis. This study evaluated the antibacterial activity of 70% ethanolic extract of Eugenia uniflora L. leaves against S. epidermidis. The leaves were extracted by maceration using 70% ethanol and subjected to phytochemical screening. Antibacterial activity was tested using the disk diffusion method at concentrations of 30%, 40%, and 50%. In addition, molecular docking analysis was performed to investigate the potential interactions of literature-reported phytochemicals with the selected bacterial molecular target. Phytochemical screening revealed the presence of tannins, saponins, and steroids. The extract showed concentration-dependent antibacterial activity with inhibition zones of 10.88, 11.60, and 12.98 mm, respectively. Molecular docking suggested a possible interaction between 2,3-di-O-galloyl-D-glucose and tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase (TyrRS), with a binding affinity of −8.8 kcal/mol. These findings suggest that E. uniflora leaf extract has potential as a natural antibacterial agent against S. epidermidis.

title: Dilemmas and Breakthroughs in Non-Core Subject Teaching in Rural Chinese Primary Schools Under the Shadow of Exam-Oriented Education
abstractText: When examination scores and school rankings dominate educational evaluation, music, art, physical education, science, and ethics and rule of law in rural primary schools are relegated to “minor” or non-core status. Drawing on teaching practicum reports and supplementary interviews in Teaching Practicum Activity Summary: Rural Schools Edition (2019–2020), this study combines literature review, purposive sampling, and thematic analysis to examine the dilemmas of non-core subject teaching under examination pressure and their underlying mechanisms. The analysis identifies five mutually reinforcing problems: displacement of scheduled lessons, specialist teacher shortages and misallocation, idle facilities with inspection-oriented paperwork, rote or unstructured teaching, and low perceived subject value among students and families. They arise not from scarce resources alone but from the interplay of score-based incentives, staffing organized around tested subjects, document-centered governance, internalized curriculum hierarchies, and reliance on short-term teaching placements as substitutes for sustainable provision. Counterexamples involving scientific inquiry, choral singing, textbook-based drama, and physical activities suggest improvement requires guaranteed curriculum implementation, county-level specialist-teacher coordination, low-cost practice-rich pedagogy, performance-based assessment, professional learning communities, and stronger home–school understanding of curriculum value. The paper argues against raising their status through high-stakes examinations; governance should instead center on students’ entitlement to actual lessons and meaningful learning.

title: Aqueous Extract of Gembili (Dioscorea esculenta) Tubers Exceeds Its Ethanol Fractions in Phenolic Content and Antioxidant Capacity
abstractText: Gembili (Dioscorea esculenta) tubers are used in Indonesia mainly as a source of inulin, recovered from hot-water extracts by ethanol precipitation, but how antioxidants partition during this step is unknown. A hot-water extract (AE) was compared with its ethanol-insoluble (EIF) and ethanol-soluble (ESF) fractions for total phenolic (TPC) and flavonoid (TFC) contents and for 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), 2,2′-azinobis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS), and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) activities. AE had the highest TPC (214.9 ± 6.1 mg gallic acid equivalents/g) and TFC (159.7 ± 6.5 mg quercetin equivalents/g), the lowest IC50 values (DPPH 30.0 ± 0.8; ABTS 28.5 ± 1.9 µg/mL), and the highest FRAP (269 ± 42 mg ascorbic acid equivalents/g). EIF exceeded ESF in all assays except FRAP (p < 0.001), and antioxidant capacity followed TPC across nine determinations (DPPH IC50, r = −0.94). The inulin-rich precipitate therefore retains part of the antioxidant capacity of the tuber.

title: Understanding the structural withdrawal of fathers from early childhood education: A PRISMA-inspired systematic review and ecological framework
abstractText: This critical integrative review examines structural and institutional constraints on paternal involvement in early childhood education (ECE), drawing on literature published between 2016 and 2026, identified through database, citation, and official-source searches, and on earlier foundational sources. Structural withdrawal is used as an analytical term for recurrent restrictions on, or uneven allocation of, fathers’ engagement, accessibility, and responsibility; it does not imply a measured decline over time. Ecological systems, social role, and work–family perspectives are used to interpret relationships among employment conditions, school practices, household care arrangements, and caregiving expectations. International findings are distinguished from Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and United Arab Emirates (UAE) evidence. The synthesis identifies five themes: working time and leave, the gendered division of care, cultural constructions of fatherhood, school communication practices, and Gulf household and residence arrangements. UAE workplace studies describe both organizational support and practical constraints, while Emirati shared-reading reports document educational engagement among participating fathers; together, these findings qualify assumptions of uniform flexibility, stigma, or disengagement. Paid domestic care is treated as one household configuration whose implications depend on task allocation and family resources. The resulting UAE-focused ecological framework proposes three pathways, through usable caregiving time, access to educational information, and the allocation of recurring responsibility, each conditioned by citizenship, residence, occupation, and household resources. Policy implications prioritize access to existing leave and workplace support and locally evaluated school measures. The evidence does not establish national prevalence or causal effects.

title: Evaluation of In Vitro Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitory Potential in Ficus adenosperma Warb. Leaf Extracts Using the Ellman Method
abstractText: Alzheimer's disease involves progressive loss of nerve cell function and affected about 50 million people worldwide in 2018, a figure projected to triple by 2050. Current acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors cause nausea and gastrointestinal disturbance, so natural alternatives are being sought. This study evaluated the AChE inhibitory activity of Ficus adenosperma Warb. leaf extracts prepared by sequential reflux extraction with n-hexane, ethyl acetate and ethanol, using the Ellman assay. The n-hexane extract yielded the highest total phenolic content (43.85 ± 3.48 mg GAE/g extract), while the ethyl acetate extract showed the highest total flavonoid content (114.27 ± 10.59 mg QE/g extract) and the greatest AChE inhibitory activity (IC50 = 1776 μg/mL). Pearson correlation analysis showed a positive but statistically non-significant association between total flavonoid content and AChE inhibition (r = 0.99, p = 0.10, n = 3). These preliminary findings suggest that flavonoids may contribute to the observed in vitro inhibition.

title: Traditional Medicine Use and Pharmacist Involvement Among Patients with Diabetes and Hypertension in Semarang, Indonesia: A Cross-sectional Study
abstractText: Patients with diabetes or hypertension often take traditional medicine alongside prescribed drugs, yet little is known about how they involve pharmacists in that use. This descriptive cross-sectional study enrolled 110 adult users of traditional medicine, recruited by purposive sampling at a community health centre and a private clinic in Semarang, Indonesia, and surveyed them with a structured questionnaire. Their mean age was 59.5 ± 10.3 years, 77.3% were women and 73.6% had diabetes. Ginger (40.9%), turmeric (39.1%) and Indonesian bay leaf (34.5%) were the remedies named most often. Pharmacists were seldom involved: 78.2% of respondents had never discussed their remedies with a pharmacist, 81.8% had never asked a pharmacist for information about them and 78.2% had never reported a side effect to one. Meanwhile, 46.4% always or often combined remedies with prescribed drugs without consulting a doctor. Community pharmacists are well placed to close this counselling gap.

title: Efectos de las prácticas de remoción de arbustos en sistemas ganaderos del Chaco Árido, Argentina
abstractText: 1. El aumento de la abundancia de arbustos nativos, impulsado por factores como la tala intensiva y el sobrepastoreo, afecta a bosques y pastizales. En el Chaco Árido, este proceso reduce el forraje. Para compensar, se remueven los arbustos y se siembran pastos exóticos. Sin embargo, se conocen poco los efectos de estas prácticas sobre la estructura de la vegetación y la relación entre pastos y leñosas. 2. Evaluamos los efectos del rolado y del desarbustado manual sobre la cobertura de árboles, arbustos y pastos, la estructura poblacional de las leñosas y la relación entre su densidad y la cobertura de pastos. Consideramos cuatro tipos de cobertura del suelo: bosque de referencia, arbustal degradado, rolado y desarbustado manual (los dos últimos, sembrados con Cenchrus ciliaris L.).3. El rolado y el desarbustado manual presentaron menor cobertura arbórea que el bosque de referencia y difirieron entre sí en arbustos y pastos. El desarbustado manual presentó menor cobertura arbustiva y mayor cobertura de pastos. El rolado presentó valores intermedios de pastos y cobertura arbustiva similar al bosque de referencia y al arbustal degradado. El bosque de referencia mostró mayor densidad de plántulas arbóreas y, junto con el arbustal degradado, mayor densidad de árboles adultos. Respecto de los arbustos, los adultos presentaron menor densidad bajo el desarbustado manual.4. La cobertura de pastos disminuyó al aumentar la densidad de leñosas, que explicó el 61% de su variación. El modelo segmentado identificó un cambio de pendiente en 1527±314 individuos leñosos/ha, disminuyendo marcadamente por debajo de este valor. La relación fue más fuerte con los arbustos adultos (R²=0.59) que con los árboles (R²=0.30).5. Implicancias. El desarbustado manual favorece los pastos, pero simplifica la vegetación leñosa. El rolado permite una mayor coexistencia entre ambos estratos, aunque sin recuperar el componente arbóreo.

title: Hemoglobinopathy diagnosis in LMICs: from hematological screening to molecular confirmation
abstractText: Hemoglobinopathy diagnosis in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) is limited not only by access to technology but also by attrition between screening, phenotypic resolution, molecular confirmation, counseling, and linkage to care. India illustrates this problem: national guidance distributes screening, high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and molecular services across district, regional, and tertiary levels, making inter-facility referral intrinsic when advanced testing is unavailable locally. Families may consequently face test charges, travel, wage loss, repeat sampling, delayed results, and incomplete partner or family testing. This Mini Review integrates evidence from India with diagnostic models from Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Indonesia, and Ghana. We examine hematological triage, the limitations of HPLC and electrophoretic methods, indications for selective molecular testing, and the structural, financial, and sociocultural causes of late or incomplete diagnosis. We propose a three-level diagnostic model supported by standardized interpretive reporting, specimen networks, active recall, local-language counseling, and measurable completion indicators. The objective is not universal sequencing, but reliable conversion of every abnormal screen into an actionable individual and familial diagnosis, supported by cascade screening and selective molecular confirmation of rare or complex genotypes that cannot be resolved phenotypically cannot be resolved phenotypically.

title: The evolution of Japan's knowledge infrastructure in the era of open access
abstractText: Abstract In 2021, CiNii—Japan's largest academic information retrieval platform—launched CiNii Research as a unified search engine, gradually integrating and upgrading its modules for articles, books, doctoral dissertations, and research projects. This paper outlines the evolution of CiNii: (1) the infrastructure phase of the NACSIS system (1983–2004), (2) the startup and expansion phase of the CiNii platform (2005–2020), and (3) the integration and upgrade phase of the CiNii Research engine (2021–). It summarizes the key features of CiNii Research, including the expansion of its search scope, optimization of search logic, and advanced English-language search capabilities. Furthermore, by examining the government-led, public-interest platform's commitment to content integration and open access, this paper discusses the implications of these upgrades for academic information services in China's higher education sector.

title: PENGEMBANGAN COURSE TERINTEGRASI AI BERBASIS PROBLEM BASED LEARNING UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KEMAMPUAN PENERAPAN PROSEDUR DAN PEMECAHAN MASALAH SISWA SMP
abstractText: ABSTRACT Informatics education requires instructional designs that connect conceptual understanding with procedural application and contextual problem-solving. This study aimed to develop an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-integrated course based on Problem-Based Learning (PBL) to support these two competencies among junior high school students. The product was developed using the Moodle platform by combining digital learning materials, problem-based activities, and AI support in the form of explanations and learning-material summaries. The needs analysis involved 113 students, while the learning-outcome evaluation employed an experimental group and a control group, each consisting of 34 students, using pretests and posttests. The needs analysis revealed percentages of 23% for decomposition, 50% for pattern recognition, 35% for abstraction, and 44% for algorithms. In procedural application of computational thinking, the experimental group's mean score increased from 58.40 to 82.60, whereas the control group's mean score increased from 57.90 to 70.30. For contextual problem-solving, the experimental group's mean score increased from 56.80 to 83.10, while the control group's mean score rose from 57.20 to 71.40. Descriptively, the experimental group demonstrated greater improvement in both measured competencies. These findings indicate the potential of the developed AI-integrated PBL course to support Informatics learning; however, its statistical effectiveness must be confirmed through inferential testing. ABSTRAK Pembelajaran Informatika membutuhkan rancangan pembelajaran yang mampu menghubungkan pemahaman konsep dengan penerapan prosedur dan penyelesaian masalah kontekstual. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan course terintegrasi Artificial Intelligence (AI) berbasis Problem-Based Learning (PBL) untuk mendukung kedua kemampuan tersebut pada siswa SMP. INTEGRASI EMPAT MATA PELAJARAN PENDIDIKAN AGAMA ISLAM (AL QUR'AN HADITS, FIQIH, AQIDAH AKHLAQ, SEJARAH KEBUDAYAAN ISLAM) DALAM KURIKULUM TRANSFORMATIF DI MADRASAH IBTIDA’IYAH
abstractText: The development of a transformative Islamic Religious Education (PAI) curriculum in Madrasah Ibtidaiyah (MI) has become an urgent imperative to counter doctrinal formalism and verbalistic learning among primary school learners. This study aims to analyze the paradigm of transformative PAI curriculum development across four core subjects (Quran-Hadith, Aqidah-Akhlaq, Fiqh, and Islamic Cultural History) by integrating curriculum characteristics, knowledge structures, objectives, approaches, instructional strategies, and pedagogical models. This qualitative library research applied content analysis to curriculum policy documents, developmental cognitive psychology literature, and transformative pedagogy theories. The findings demonstrate that transformative PAI curricula at the MI level cultivate prophetic values through reflective habituation aligned with children's concrete operational developmental stage. The epistemological structure connects religious texts with students' daily social experiences through an integrative-interconnective paradigm. A contextual-humanistic approach paired with role-modeling strategies and experiential learning models successfully shifts PAI goals from procedural memorization to the internalization of inclusive socio-religious conduct.

Digital Technology Integration and Academic Performance in Tertiary Mathematics: A Meta-Analytic Review of Pedagogy and Learning Results
abstractText: This study aims to assess the influence of digital technologies on undergraduate mathematics performance. A meta-analytic approach was employed, synthesized from 26 independent samples across 17 peer-reviewed articles (1990–2025), with a cumulative sample size of 2,010 participants. The findings indicate a large overall effect size (g=0.978), suggesting that digital technologies significantly enhance academic achievement compared to traditional instructional methods. Moderator analysis indicated that blended learning environments achieved the highest effect size; furthermore, the impact of digital technology integration on academic performance was most pronounced in the fields of Trigonometry and Calculus. Additionally, mathematics-specific software was found to exert a significant influence on the observed effect sizes. Furthermore, the use of standardized assessments yielded a smaller effect size compared to instructor-designed tests. Additionally, no significant differences were observed regarding student equivalence in terms of group composition. The study concludes that the impact of digital tools is contingent upon specific moderator variables; these factors should be integrated into instructional design to optimize learning outcomes in university mathematics.

title: Efek Ekstrak Bonggol Nanas Madu (Ananas comosus L. Merr) terhadap Penurunan Jumlah Sel Plasma pada Gingivitis Tikus Wistar
abstractText: Gingivitis is an inflammatory condition of the gingival tissue characterized by the presence of inflammatory cells, including plasma cells that play a role in the immune response. The pineapple core extract (Ananas comosus L. Merr) contains bioactive compounds such as bromelain and flavonoids that have potential as anti-inflammatory agents. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of pineapple core extract (Ananas comosus L. Merr) at concentrations of 12.5% and 25% on the number of plasma cells in the gingival tissue of Wistar rats with histologically confirmed gingivitis, and to determine the concentration that produced the greatest reduction in the number of plasma cells. A laboratory experimental study using a post-test only control group design was conducted on Wistar rats, which were divided into control and treatment groups administered pineapple core extract at concentrations of 12.5% and 25%. Gingivitis was induced using ligation, followed by the preparation of histological sections stained with hematoxylin-eosin to observe plasma cell counts using a light microscope. Data were analyzed using Tukey’s HSD post hoc test. The treatment group showed a lower number of plasma cells compared to the control group with a statistically significant difference (p < 0.05), where the 25% concentration showed a greater reduction compared to 12.5%. The pineapple core extract demonstrates an effect in reducing the number of plasma cells in gingivitis in Wistar rats.

A robust visual localization framework for UAVs using a zero-shot aerial-satellite image matcher and a particle filter
abstractText: Abstract Positioning of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) normally relies on the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). However, GNSS signals are prone to blockage, interference, and spoofing, which can cause positioning failures and severely degrade mission performance. Aerial-satellite image matching using intelligent methods (e.g., deep neural networks) has emerged as a promising approach for achieving meter-level absolute positioning accuracy in GNSS-denied environments. To advance localization based on aerial-satellite image matching, we propose a robust localization framework that integrates a zero-shot aerial-satellite image matcher, termed the Generalizable Image Matcher (GIM), with a particle filter. First, the front-end visual odometry estimates the UAV trajectory from consecutive onboard images to produce an initial pose. Next, guided by the front-end estimate, candidate locations are sampled to crop the corresponding satellite sub-images. GIM is then used to match aerial and satellite images and infer absolute location cues. Finally, an adaptive weighting function is designed to fuse the front-end and back-end localization information, thereby yielding the final positioning result. Experiments were conducted using data collected along 12 flight trajectories spanning rural, urban, and farmland scenarios. Assuming that the initial position of each trajectory is known, the proposed method achieved an overall average positioning error of 5.02 m across all 12 trajectories, with average errors of 5.46 m for the nine real-data trajectories and 3.69 m for the three synthetic-data trajectories. Across the evaluated trajectories, which covered a cumulative flight distance of 104,566 m, no accumulation of positioning drift was observed. These results indicate stable positioning performance under the outdoor datasets and experimental conditions evaluated in this study.

title: Indonesian Medicinal Plants Investigated for Cancer-Related Activity: A Review of Ethnobotanical, Phytochemical, and Preclinical Evidence
abstractText: Medicinal plants are widely used by Indonesian cancer patients, but the evidence behind this use differs in kind and strength. This review classified 24 studies from Google Scholar, ScienceDirect and PubMed, plus ten further primary studies, by evidence level: traditional use, general toxicity, cancer-cell cytotoxicity, measured mechanism, in silico prediction and compound identification. Cancer-cell data existed for 15 of 17 taxa, almost all as crude extracts, and normal-cell controls were rare. The lowest IC50 values were 23.7 µg/mL (Caulerpa racemosa hexane extract, MCF-7) and 54.48 µg/mL (Zanthoxylum acanthopodium fruit ethanol extract, 4T1). The name bajakah covered species of three genera. Mechanisms were measured only for curcumin, Stenochlaena palustris and Ocimum tenuiflorum, and no in vivo efficacy study was found. Botanical authentication, selectivity testing, compound isolation and animal studies should precede therapeutic claims.

title: A Comparison of Tensile Testing Techniques and Predictive Correlations
abstractText: Abstract The engineering properties of a rock foundation are key parameters in the analysis of dams as they inform an understanding of how a structure will perform under a loading condition of interest. One important, but difficult to accurately evaluate, engineering property is the tensile strength of rock. As the direct tensile strength (DTS) testing of intact rock is non-trivial and expensive, the tensile strength is typically inferred from more common indirect methods, such as the Brazilian tensile strength (BTS) test, akin to the splitting tensile strength test performed on concrete, or using correlations to other mechanical properties, such as the crack initiation (CI) strength, m i parameter from the Generalized Hoek-Brown failure criterion, or the Mode I fracture toughness. This research leverages a robust laboratory testing program utilizing a state-of-the-art digital image correlation (DIC) system to understand how the different platen shapes and the use of a soft cushion affect BTS results, improve the understanding about the relationship between DTS and BTS tests (with a specific focus on optimizing the test arrangement), and explores correlations between other laboratory-measured properties (e.g., CI and m i ) and the DTS. The DTS was difficult to measure directly, but was found to be closely related to the BTS when testing was performed using curved platens, with or without a cushion; this testing arrangement also resulted in a failure mechanism that aligns with the underlying assumptions from Hondros (1959); ISRM (1978); and ASTM (2016). When analyzing the BTS data from different platen arrangements, it is important to use a relationship that incorporates the loading arc angle to ensure data are comparable as the BTS is a function of the loading arc angle in the full stress solution. The use of CI or m i to estimate the DTS was found to be unreliable with the BTS providing the closest approximation

title: Microbial–chemical amendment promotes phosphorus mobilization during kitchen-waste biomass valorization
PENERAPAN MODEL KOOPERATIF TIPE NUMBERED HEAD TOGETHER DALAM MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA MURID KELAS IV
abstractText: The learning outcomes of fourth-grade students in Pancasila Education at UPTD SD Negeri 074048 Luaha Bouso were still low because previous learning tended to be teacher-centered, resulting in limited student activity, collaboration, and participation. This study aimed to describe the implementation of the Numbered Head Together (NHT) cooperative learning model and to determine the improvement of students' learning outcomes in Pancasila Education after its implementation. The study employed Classroom Action Research using the Kemmis and McTaggart model and was conducted in two cycles. Each cycle consisted of planning, action, observation, and reflection, with two meetings in each cycle. The subjects were 19 fourth-grade students in the 2025/2026 academic year. Data were collected through observations of teacher and student activities, learning outcome tests, documentation, and field notes, and were analyzed descriptively using qualitative and quantitative approaches. The NHT implementation involved heterogeneous group formation, assigning numbers to group members, presenting questions or tasks, group discussion, random number calling, presentation of answers, and reinforcement. The findings showed that teacher activity increased from 58% in Cycle I Meeting I to 90% in Cycle II Meeting II, while student activity increased from 57.69% to 94.23%. Learning outcomes also improved, as indicated by an increase in the mean score from 62.68 in Cycle I to 80.63 in Cycle II and classical mastery from 47.37% to 84.21%. Therefore, the implementation of NHT improved student participation and learning outcomes in Pancasila Education.

title: From pathogen burden to host response: complement remodeling as a marker of TB activity
abstractText: Abstract Tuberculosis (TB) progression is shaped by host inflammatory remodeling, not only by pathogen burden. Here, we investigated whether peripheral complement dysregulation represents a host-response program associated with tuberculosis disease activity, disease severity, and clinical outcomes. We integrated public peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) transcriptomic data, clinical qRT-PCR validation, serum complement profiling, single-cell transcriptomics, flow cytometry, and 6-month outcome assessment. A treatment-responsive C1q-centered classical complement module emerged across datasets: C1q-related genes were increased in active TB, decreased after anti-TB treatment, and were further enriched in severe disease. Clinical PBMC analyses confirmed increased C1r, C1QB, and CR2 in active TB and enrichment of C1r, C1QB, and C1QC in severe TB. At the serum level, increased C1q and soluble membrane attack complex (sMAC), together with reduced soluble complement receptor 2 (sCR2), were consistent with complement activation and altered complement receptor-related regulation; CD46 was also increased in severe disease. Complement-related measures tracked systemic inflammatory and clinical indices, while associations with 6-month outcome provided additional evidence linking this response to disease progression. Single-cell and flow cytometry analyses localized complement-associated signals mainly to monocyte populations within a myeloid-skewed inflammatory landscape. Collectively, these findings suggest that peripheral complement remodeling represents a monocyte-linked inflammatory host-response feature associated with tuberculosis progression. Parenting in the Digital Age: Parents’ Experiences of Primary School Children’s Technology Use
abstractText: This study aimed to examine in depth the digital parenting experiences of parents who had children attending primary school. The study was conducted as a case study within a qualitative research approach. The participants were 12 parents whose children were enrolled in Grades 1-4 during the 2022-2023 academic year. Data were collected through a personal information form and an open-ended interview form and were analyzed using descriptive analysis. Four main themes were identified, digital tools in children's lives, parental responses to children's digital tool use, the perceived effects of digital tools on children, and parents' own digital tool use. The findings showed that children were introduced to digital tools at approximately age two and commonly used smartphones, television, and tablets. Although parents supported children's beneficial use of digital tools, they were concerned about their children's possible exposure to risky situations in digital environments. Parents most often described themselves as having a guiding role in children's digital tool use, while some also emphasized consistency and tolerance in parenting behavior.

title: Influence of Refractive Error and Axial Length on Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer Thickness Assessed by Optical Coherence Tomography
abstractText: Purpose: To investigate the influence of refractive status and axial length on Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer (RNFL) thickness as measured by Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT). Methods: This cross-sectional study included 116 eyes from 62 participants. Peripapillary RNFL thickness was assessed using the TOPCON 3D OCT-2000 system. Comparisons of RNFL thickness were performed among hyperopic, emmetropic and myopic eyes and the relationship between axial length and RNFL thickness was analyzed. Results: Compared with emmetropic eyes, the hyperopic group demonstrated no statistically significant increase in average RNFL thickness or in the superior, inferior, nasal and temporal quadrants (p = 0.760, 0.160, 0.139, 0.345 and 0.762, respectively). Similarly, the myopic group showed no significant reduction in average RNFL thickness or in any quadrant compared with the emmetropic group (p = 0.991, 0.746, 0.848, 0.382 and 0.894, respectively). A significant inverse relationship was observed between axial length and RNFL thickness. Increasing axial length was associated with a reduction in average RNFL thickness as well as in the superior, inferior and nasal quadrants (p = 0.0009, p = 0.0003, p = 0.0031 and p = 0.0129, respectively). No significant association was found between axial length and temporal quadrant RNFL thickness (p = 0.8118). Conclusion: Refractive status alone, whether myopic or hyperopic, did not significantly influence RNFL thickness measurements. In contrast, increased axial length was associated with significant thinning of the RNFL in the average, superior, inferior and nasal quadrants, while the temporal quadrants remained unaffected. These findings highlight the importance of considering axial length when interpreting RNFL measurements obtained by OCT.

title: Effectiveness of Ethanol Extract of Kluwih (Artocarpus camansi) Leaves on Total Cholesterol in Rats Given a High-Fat Diet and Streptozotocin
abstractText: Leaves of Artocarpus camansi (kluwih) are used in Indonesian folk medicine, but their effect on blood lipids, which are often disturbed in type 2 diabetes, is untested in vivo. This study evaluated an ethanol extract of A. camansi leaves in rats given a high-fat diet followed by low-dose streptozotocin. Thirty male rats formed six groups (n = 5): normal, vehicle, simvastatin, and extract at 300, 350 or 400 mg/kg daily for 14 days. Total cholesterol, measured on days 0, 14, 21, 28 and 35, rose from 43–48 to 127–141 mg/dL after induction. The extract then lowered it by a mean of 57.2%, 48.0% and 43.5% at the three doses, against 64.9% for simvastatin, while vehicle rats kept rising (group × time interaction, p < 0.001). At 300 mg/kg, final total cholesterol (53.4 ± 5.1 mg/dL) did not differ from the normal or simvastatin groups. Its active constituents remain unquantified.

title: Effect of Red Galangal–Citronella Grass Decoction Ratios on Phenolic Content, Flavonoid Content, and Antioxidant Activity
abstractText: Whether the plants in polyherbal decoctions interact is rarely tested. Red galangal (Alpinia purpurata) and citronella grass (Cymbopogon nardus) were decocted at ratios of 100:0, 75:25, 50:50, 25:75, and 0:100 (w/w) and analysed for total phenolic content (TPC), total flavonoid content (TFC), and 2,2′-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS) radical-scavenging activity; mixtures were compared with additive expectations. TPC decreased from 593.84 to 375.75 mg gallic acid equivalents/L as citronella grass increased, whereas TFC peaked at 25:75 (49.90 mg quercetin equivalents/L). The half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC₅₀) ranged from 1106.64 µg/mL (red galangal) to 1682.97 µg/mL (citronella grass). Every mixture’s activity matched the additive prediction (observed/expected 0.96–1.05, p > 0.3), whereas TFC deviated strongly (0.74–1.41). Activity correlated with TPC (r = 0.97, p = 0.007) but not TFC. The ratio therefore adjusts antioxidant capacity proportionally, without synergy, and phenolics rather than flavonoids govern it.

The Development of the SONICC Learning Model Assisted by Augmented Reality Media in Elementary Science Education
abstractText: This study developed, validated, tested the practicality, and examined the effectiveness of the SONICC learning model assisted by augmented reality media in elementary science education for students in an Elementary School Teacher Education Study Program. The study used a research and development design based on the Borg and Gall model. The development process produced a SONICC learning model with six syntax stages: Setting Goals, Organization, New Idea, Innovation, Critical and Creative Thinking, and Communication. It also produced five supporting products: a learning model book, teaching material book, lecturer guidebook, student guidebook, and augmented reality media guidebook. Data were collected using validation sheets, practicality questionnaires, documentation, and learning outcome tests. The validation results reached an average score of 92.30% with a validity value of 3.69, indicating a very valid category. The practicality results reached 94.27% with a practicality value of 3.66, indicating a very practical category. The effectiveness test showed an N-Gain score of 78.78%, which was categorized as effective. These findings show that the SONICC learning model assisted by augmented reality media is valid, practical, and effective for improving elementary science learning in higher education.

title: Red Palm Oil Administration in Undernourished Wistar Rats: Effects on Cognitive, Gastrointestinal, Skeletal, and Organ Parameters
abstractText: Background: Malnutrition affects multiple physiological systems, including cognitive, gastrointestinal, skeletal, and organ functions. Red palm oil (RPO) contains bioactive compounds that may influence physiological responses to malnutrition. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of RPO on biomedical parameters in undernourished Wistar rats. Methods: This experimental laboratory study integrated several sub-studies using post-test-only and pretest-posttest control group designs. Male Wistar rats aged 3–4 weeks underwent 50% feed restriction for 14 days, followed by RPO administration at doses of 2, 4, or 6 mL/kgBW for 28 days. Groups included normal, negative, and selected positive vitamin A controls. Sample sizes varied across sub-studies. Data were analyzed using ANOVA, Kruskal– Wallis, post hoc tests, and correlation analyses, with p < 0.05 considered significant. Result: Significant differences were observed in Y-maze cognitive performance (p = 0.031), intestinal weight (p = 0.003), femur weight (ANOVA p = 0.037; Kruskal–Wallis p = 0.048), and heart (p = 0.010), liver (p = 0.002), and kidney (p = 0.004) indices. Femur length differed significantly using Kruskal–Wallis (p = 0.042), but not ANOVA (p = 0.052). No significant differences were observed in hemoglobin levels (p = 0.494),motor performance (p = 0.120), lung (p = 0.070), or spleen (p = 0.120) indices. Contribution for Practice: RPO administration produced variable responses across biomedical parameters, providing preliminary preclinical evidence for further nutritional research. However, inconsistent dose-response patterns and the absence of significant effects on several outcomes limit its clinical applicability. Further mechanistic and clinical studies are required before RPO can be recommended for nutritional rehabilitation.

Pergeseran Penggunaan Bahasa Indonesia Baku Ke Bahasa Slang Gen Z (Brainrot) Dan Dampaknya Terhadap Komunikasi Akademik
abstractText: This study is motivated by the shift from standard Indonesian to Generation Z’s slang, known as brainrot, and its potential impact on academic communication in higher education settings. Terms such as skibidi, mewing, yapping, sigma, and rizz, which originally gained popularity in digital spaces, have begun to permeate students’ spoken interactions, potentially blurring the boundary between informal and formal academic discourse. This research aims to describe the forms and functions of brainrot vocabulary in students’ speech, map the academic interaction domains vulnerable to interference, and analyze students’ perceptions of language norm compliance and its effect on the clarity of scientific communication. This study employs a qualitative descriptive approach grounded in sociolinguistic study, with data collected through an online survey of 20 active students from the Indonesian Language and Literature Education Program at Universitas Pekalongan, class of 2025, as well as the uninvolved observation method (simak bebas libat cakap) during actual classroom situations. The results show that the term brainrot is already recognized by 86% of respondents, with yapping (37%), bro (28%), and mewing (15%) reported as the most frequently used terms. Their use is concentrated in casual conversations among peers (91%), while usage in formal academic domains such as presentations and communication with lecturers is nearly absent. As many as 71% of respondents consider the use of brainrot inappropriate in academic contexts, and 86% believe the term can affect the clarity of scientific communication. These findings indicate that students generally remain able to distinguish language varieties according to context, suggesting that the shift toward brainrot slang does not yet pose a significant threat to academic communication, although the tendency toward interference still warrants attention as part of the linguistic dynamics of the digital generation.

title: Long-lived quantum memories with rare-earth ions doped in crystals
abstractText: Abstract Quantum memory is a core enabling device for large-scale quantum networks, serving as the fundamental building block for quantum repeaters and transportable quantum memories. Among various physical platforms, rare-earth-ion-doped crystals stand out as one of the most promising solid-state candidates for long-lived photonic quantum memories, owing to their exceptionally long spin coherence time and their compatibility with integration. In this review, we first introduce the physical mechanisms underlying long-lived spin coherence in rare-earth systems, with particular emphasis on the zero-first-order-Zeeman transition and dynamical decoupling techniques. We then review the experimental progress in this field, highlighting three distinct lifetimes—the spin coherence time, the light storage time, and the quantum storage time—and covering experiments that have achieved hour-scale spin coherence, minute- to hour-scale light storage, and minute-scale single-photon-level quantum storage. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges that hinder the realization of practical long-lived quantum memories, explore potential strategies to overcome these obstacles, and outline the prospects for their future applications in quantum networks.

title: Modeling the evolution of subtraction schemes in low-resource contexts: A two-time Markov transition analysis of persistent errors and learning trajectories
Status Gizi Ibu Selama Kehamilan Sebagai Determinan Stunting Dan Early Childhood Caries Pada Anak Usia 12–59 Bulan Di Kabupaten Sidoarjo
abstractText: Stunting and early childhood caries (ECC) remain major health problems among young children in Indonesia. Maternal nutritional status during pregnancy influences fetal growth and the formation of primary tooth enamel, yet evidence that examines maternal nutrition, stunting, and ECC within the same population remains limited.The aim of this research is to analyse the association between maternal nutritional status during pregnancy, assessed by mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), and the occurrence of stunting and ECC among children aged 12–59 months in Sidoarjo Regency. This analytic observational study used a cross-sectional design with retrospective maternal record tracing and involved 103 mother–child pairs recruited from community health posts (Posyandu). First-trimester MUAC was obtained from the Maternal and Child Health (KIA) book, and MUAC <23.5 cm was classified as chronic energy deficiency (CED). Stunting was defined as a height-for-age Z-score below −2 SD according to the WHO Child Growth Standards, and ECC as a deft score ≥1. Data were analysed using the chi-square and binary logistic regression adjusted for child age and sex. CED was identified in 14.6% of mothers. The prevalence of stunting was 20.8% (n=101) and that of ECC was 63.1%, with a mean deft of 3.50 ± 3.80 dominated by the decayed component. Stunting was more frequent among children of mothers with CED (46.7% vs 16.3%; p=0.014; adjusted OR 6.83; 95% CI 1.54–30.25). Maternal CED was not associated with ECC (p=0.153; adjusted OR 1.02; 95% CI 0.28–3.76), whereas older child age was (adjusted OR 1.06 per month; 95% CI 1.02–1.11). Stunting and ECC were not significantly associated (p=0.447), and mediation analysis showed no significant indirect effect of maternal CED on ECC through stunting. Maternal CED during pregnancy was associated with stunting in children aged 12–59 months, whereas no direct association with ECC was found. Maternal nutritional status may influence ECC indirectly through impaired enamel formation and child growth, but this pathway was not statistically demonstrated and requires confirmation in cohort studies.

title: A deep learning-based method for enhanced prediction of long-term diaphragm wall deflections using multi-source data
abstractText: Abstract Machine learning-based autoregressive models are widely applied to deformation prediction of braced excavations, yet they often suffer from pronounced error accumulation and deteriorated accuracy in long-term forecasting. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multi-source information fusion framework for predicting diaphragm wall deformation that integrates construction information with historical wall-deflection data. By incorporating construction-related dynamic features as auxiliary inputs, the proposed model effectively strengthens long-term dependency learning and reduces the propagation of autoregressive errors. A depth-weighted loss coefficient is further introduced to prioritize accuracy in shallow regions where deformation is most critical, and a 1D U-Net decoder is employed to enhance profile-level reconstruction through multi-scale spatial feature extraction. The framework is validated using two deep excavation projects on Nanjing Metro Line 11. For excavation-induced deformation, the model demonstrates stable and accurate multi-step prediction performance for diaphragm wall deflection, even under long forecasting steps. Comparative analyses further confirm that the proposed fusion architecture provides superior long-term robustness under limited monitoring data. The results highlight the method’s potential as a practical tool for deformation forecasting and construction risk management in foundation pit engineering.

title: Digital Communication within School Public Relations Management: A Multi-Site Study of Educational Quality
abstractText: Digital communication has become an important component of school public relations because it allows faster information exchange and more direct interaction with parents and community stakeholders. This study examined public relations management at three public senior high schools in Kendari, Indonesia, with particular attention to the digital communication practices that emerged across the sites and their contribution to educational quality. A qualitative multi-site case study approach was employed. Data were obtained through in-depth interviews, non-participant observation, and document review and were analyzed within and across the three sites. WhatsApp was the main digital channel for daily school-parent communication, particularly through homeroom teachers. SMA Negeri 6 Kendari showed the most structured and collaborative communication practices, while SMA Negeri 2 Kendari depended more on individual initiatives and SMA Negeri 8 Kendari used a more situational approach. Digital communication supported information transparency, parent-school coordination, student guidance, participation, and public trust. However, access to technology alone did not ensure effective public relations. Inconsistent communication standards, short-notice messages, unequal parent responses, limited documentation, and weak follow-up reduced its effectiveness. Effective digital communication therefore depended on its integration with planning, stakeholder participation, evaluation, and continuous follow-up.

title: AI and Classroom Assessment in Pre-service Teacher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research Trends, Thematic Evolution, and Future Directions
abstractText: Assessment preparation in teacher education remains a persistent concern as pre-service teachers are increasingly expected to design valid assessments, generate meaningful feedback, interpret learning evidence, and exercise professional judgment in AI-mediated classrooms. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of research on artificial intelligence-enhanced classroom assessment in pre-service teacher education from 2005 to 2025. Using Scopus-indexed publications, the study analyzed 344 documents from 242 sources to map publication trends, citation patterns, influential authors and institutions, geographic distribution, co-citation structures, keyword co-occurrence networks, and thematic evolution. Results show that the field is young but rapidly expanding, with an annual growth rate of 29.61% and a sharp increase in publications from 2022 onward, reflecting the growing influence of generative AI, ChatGPT, automated feedback, learning analytics, and intelligent learning systems. Co-citation analysis revealed three intellectual foundations: teacher knowledge and research foundations, generative AI-mediated pedagogical practice, formative feedback and automated assessment. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identified four major thematic clusters: AI integration and ethical teacher education, intelligent learning systems and data-driven student learning, AI-supported feedback and personalization, and assessment analytics and evidence-based grading. The findings suggest that AI-enhanced classroom assessment is not merely a technological issue but a pedagogical and professional concern requiring assessment literacy, AI literacy, ethical judgment, and teacher agency. The study contributes a field-level understanding of this emerging research domain and highlights the need for more focused, ethical, and context-sensitive studies on how pre-service teachers design, evaluate, and use AI-supported classroom assessments.

Hybrid resorbable anchors/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers for enhanced pedicle screw fixation
abstractText: Pedicle screw loosening remains a challenge for surgeons and patients. We propose using hybrid resorbable anchors and drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers to enhance the bone fixation of pedicle screws. Polylactide (PLA) anchors with various designs were fabricated using additive manufacturing, while simvastatin- and bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanofibers were prepared through coaxial electrospinning. The effects of PLA anchors and drug/biomolecule-loaded PLGA nanofibrous membranes on improving the pullout strength of pedicle screws from artificial bones were investigated. The in vitro release characteristics of simvastatin and BMP-2 from the nanofibers were evaluated using high-performance liquid chromatography and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, while the in vivo elution of simvastatin was assessed in a rabbit model with histological examinations. The results demonstrate that electrospun drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers, when wrapped around pedicle screws, enhance the screws’ pullout strength. Additionally, the nanofiber/screw system provides a sustained release of simvastatin and BMP-2 for over 30 days in vitro and 4 weeks in vivo. Histological analysis also confirmed the biocompatibility of nanofibrous anchors. Hybrid resorbable anchors and drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers show potential for improving screw fixation and serving as a platform for extended drug delivery.

title: Picloram-Induced Embryogenic Callus Formation and Proliferation from Nucellar Embryo of Mandarin ‘Berastagi’ (Citrus reticulata Blanco)
abstractText: Mandarin ‘Berastagi’ (Citrus reticulata Blanco) is a key horticultural commodity in North Sumatra, Indonesia, with increasing demand for high quality, genetically uniform planting material. Biotechnological approaches, somatic embryogenesis, hold particularly significant potential enhancing propagation efficiency and crop quality. This study aimed to determine the optimal culture medium and picloram concentration for the induction and proliferation of embryogenic callus from nucellar explants of Mandarin ‘Berastagi’ in vitro. Two experiments were conducted: (1) induction of embryogenic callus from nucellar embryos isolated from young fruits (60–70 days after anthesis) cultured on different basal media supplemented with varying picloram concentrations, and (2) proliferation of embryogenic callus on media containing different carbohydrate concentrations. The Murashige and Wetmore (MW) medium supplemented with 1.5 mg/L picloram resulted in the highest callus induction rate (37.8%) and largest mean callus diameter (17.8 mm). For proliferation, MW medium containing 4% sucrose produced the best response, with an average callus diameter of 14 mm and 96% of explants developing globular stage somatic embryos. These results establish an efficient somatic embryogenesis protocol that can support large-scale propagation and future crop improvement programs in Mandarin ‘Berastagi’.

title: Longitudinal Drought Patterns and Predictive Analysis in Lalitpur, Uttar Pradesh, India: An Application of SPI and SPEI
abstractText: Drought is a significant hydrological hazard that leaves a serious footprint on the environment, society and human life. Water resources, agricultural productivity, ecosystems, livelihoods and socio-economic well-beings are negatively impacted by drought. This make a serious footprint on the environment, society and also human lives. Nowadays, many regions of the worlds are experiencing increasing frequent and a severe drought condition. Natural climatic variability and anthropogenic factors combinedly influence the drought patterns and trends. This study investigates the spatial and temporal characteristics and variation of drought patterns in Lalitpur District of Uttar Pradesh State, India. Thirty-five years metrological data collected from the NASA POWER Access Viewer were used to fulfil the research objectives. Two drought indices, Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) were calculated 3, 6, 9 and 12 month timescales. For asses the direction and statistical significance of temporal trends, Spearman’s rank correlation method was used. Sen’s slope estimator was employed to quantifying magnitude of these trends. The result indicates the occurrence of drought over multiple years and reveals a tendency toward increasing drought severity. Variations in rainfall patterns, overuse of ground water, agricultural transformation and changes in land use pattern may be contribute to the observed of drought trends. As a result, agricultural productivity in this region is also significantly affected. Future projections for 2026–2035 indicated drought occurrence of 11.67%, 8.33%, 1.67%, and 9.17% for SPI-3, SPI-6, SPI-9, and SPI-12, respectively, while SPEI projected 5.83%, 3.33%, 1.67%, and 0.83% at the corresponding time scales. The findings highlight the importance of multi-timescale drought assessment and forecasting for effective drought monitoring, water-resource management, and agricultural planning in Lalitpur District.

title: TNF-α (rs1800629) Gene Polymorphism and Circulating Inflammatory Markers in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Case-Control Study
abstractText: Aim: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a progressive respiratory disorder characterized by persistent airflow limitation and systemic inflammation. Tumor Necrosis Factor-Alpha (TNF-α) is a key pro-inflammatory cytokine implicated in COPD pathogenesis, although the role of the TNF-α −308 G>A polymorphism remains uncertain. To evaluate the association between TNF-α −308 G>A polymorphism and COPD and to assess circulating inflammatory markers. Methods: In this case-control study, 120 participants (60 COPD patients and 60 age and sex matched controls; 25-70 years) were enrolled. TNF-α −308 G>A polymorphism was genotyped using allele-specific ARMS-PCR. Serum TNF-α, IL-4 and IL-6 were measured by ELISA. Pulmonary, haematological and biochemical parameters were compared between groups. Results: COPD patients showed significantly reduced FEV₁, FEV₁/FVC, FVC, DLCO and KCO (p<0.001), with lower BMI and albumin and higher urea and leukocyte count (p<0.05). Conclusion: TNF-α levels were marginally higher in COPD patients (p = 0.05).in COPD (p=0.05), whereas IL-4 and IL-6 were not different. The GG genotype predominated, with no association between TNF-α −308 G>A polymorphism and COPD (p=0.83). TNF-α −308 G>A polymorphism was not associated with COPD risk, but elevated TNF-α supports its role in COPD-related systemic inflammation.

title: Environment-Related Technological Innovation and Ecological Footprint in India: Aggregate and Component-Wise Time–Frequency Analysis
abstractText: This study investigates the time-frequency dynamics between environment-related technological innovation and environmental quality using the ecological footprint as a comprehensive measure of environmental quality and its components for India. To capture time-varying and frequency-dependent relationships, the study adopts a wavelet coherence framework, which allows simultaneous analysis of short-, medium-, and long-run dynamics between environment-related technological innovation and environmental quality for the period between 1990Q1 to 2022Q4. The results indicate that the relationship between environment-related technological innovation and environmental quality is strongly time-varying and scale-dependent. In the aggregate ecological footprint, the significant coherence is concentrated on the short and medium horizons, while the long-run interactions are weak and non-persistent. The phase dynamics show that the rise in ecological footprint precedes the adoption of environment-related technological innovation. In components analysis, it shows a strong short-term coherence between technological innovation in the environmental field and single parts of the ecological footprint. At the same time, the medium-run effects are intermittent, and the long-run relationships are mostly insignificant or driven by boundary effects. The results suggest that the environmental benefits from environment-related technological innovation are gradual and uneven in ecological dimensions. Therefore, policymakers should complement technology-promotion strategies with regulatory and demand-side measures to avoid overreliance on long-term technological solutions and to better address short-term ecological footprint.

title: The Effect of Generative AI and Gamification on Enhancing Students’ Motivation Based on the ARCS Model
abstractText: High school biology learning is often hindered by abstract concepts and cognitive overload, leading to low student motivation. Although generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and gamification show instructional potential, their combined motivational effects remain underexplored. Grounded in the ARCS model, this study examined the impact of integrating ChatGPT-based GenAI and gamification on students’ Attention, Relevance, Confidence, and Satisfaction. A longitudinal quasi-experimental repeated measures design was conducted with 52 high school biology students over eight weeks. Motivation was measured at four time points using a validated ARCS questionnaire and analyzed with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results showed significant improvements across all ARCS dimensions from pre- to post-intervention (p < .001). Attention and relevance increased steadily, confidence improved in later stages, and satisfaction rose overall. Reported challenges included limited personalized AI feedback, competition-induced anxiety associated with leaderboard-based competition, and increased cognitive load resulting from complex AI-generated content. The findings indicate that GenAI-supported gamification can enhance motivation in biology learning when supported by careful pedagogical design.

title: Full-fat soybean origin and thermal processing affect protein secondary structure, in vitro digestion kinetics, and predicted standardized ileal amino acid digestibility in broiler chickens
abstractText: Abstract Background This study evaluated the chemical composition, protein secondary structure, crude protein (CP) solubilization, and in-vitro amino acid (AA) digestibility of three Kenyan full-fat soybean (FFSB) samples (S1, S2, S3) with unknown processing histories and compared with Canadian samples: raw FFSB, extruded FFSB at 160.0 °C, and FFSB roasted at 136.7 °C, 151.7 °C, or 154.4 °C. Protein structure was characterized using attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. A two-phase in-vitro digestion model was used to determine CP solubilization and AA digestibility. Observed in-vivo standardized ileal digestibility (SID) values from a study using FFSB roasted at 136.7 °C were regressed on corresponding in-vitro AA digestibility values to generate predicted SID values. Results Thermal processing reduced trypsin inhibitor activity (TIA) in Canadian FFSB from 17.42 TIU/mg in raw FFSB to 3.85 TIU/mg in extruded FFSB and to 4.77, 4.59, and 2.30 TIU/mg in samples roasted at 136.7, 151.7, and 154.4 °C, respectively. In contrast, Kenyan Samples 1, 2, and 3 had residual TIA values of 8.00, 6.00, and 12.00 TIU/mg, respectively. Protein secondary structure differed among samples ( P < 0.001), with the 136.7 °C-roasted sample having greater aggregated β-sheet and β-turn contents and lower random coil content than most samples. CP solubilization differed among samples at each digestion time point ( P < 0.001). At the end of the intestinal phase, processed Canadian samples had greater CP solubilization than raw FFSB but did not differ from one another, whereas Kenyan Samples 2 and 3 were comparable to Canadian raw FFSB. In-vitro AA digestibility differed among samples for all AA ( P ≤ 0.001). For mean total AA digestibility, the 154.4 °C and 151.7 °C-roasted sample had the highest digestibility; Kenyan Sample 1 was greater than Samples 2 and 3, and Sample 3 did not differ from raw FFSB. The regression model showed agreement at the mean level but larger prediction errors for lysine, aspartic acid, and proline, indicating AA-specific limitations. Conclusions Overall, processing conditions and ingredient origin influenced FFSB quality, with roasting at 151.7–154.4 °C producing favorable structural and digestibility responses. The variability observed among Kenyan samples highlights the need for routine quality assessment of commercial FFSB before feed formulation.

Anti-anemic Potential of Parkia speciosa Hassk. Peel Extract in Sodium Nitrite-Induced Anemic Wistar Rats: Evaluation of Hematological Parameters
abstractText: Anemia involves reduced hemoglobin, erythrocyte count and hematocrit, often with oxidative damage to erythrocytes. Petai (Parkia speciosa Hassk.) peel is underused waste with hematoprotective compounds. This study tested its anti-anemic potential in sodium nitrite-induced rats. Thirty male rats formed six groups of five (three analysed): normal, negative and positive controls (ferrous fumarate), and extract at 300, 400 and 500 mg/kg BW. Sodium nitrite 50 mg/kg BW ran 14 days, the extract orally in the last seven. Hematology was measured on days 0 and 14. Phytochemical screening revealed alkaloids, flavonoids, saponins, tannins and steroids. The extract improved hemoglobin, erythrocyte count and hematocrit at all doses; the highest raised leukocytes markedly (50.14 ± 17.89 ×10³/μL), possibly an inflammatory or stress response. The 300 mg/kg BW dose was optimal.

title: Revealing a pressure-induced reversible polymorph transformation by monitoring in-die density during powder compression
abstractText: Abstract The reversible pressure-induced phase transformation of urea during powder compaction was investigated using a compaction simulator. The reversible change in solid density observed between 600 MPa and 900 MPa is consistent with the known pressure-induced reversible phase transformation between urea forms I and III. These findings establish compaction simulation as a material-sparing method for detecting pressure-induced phase transformations of active pharmaceutical ingredients during tableting, provided that the density change due to the polymorphic form transition is sufficiently large.

title: Development of a scalable radiative cooling coating with sustained sub-ambient performance in outdoor environments
Effectiveness of Octopus (Octopus sp.) Ink Extract on the Growth of Catfish (Clarias sp.) Infected with Staphylococcus aureus
abstractText: Catfish (Clarias sp.) is an economically important freshwater aquaculture commodity in Indonesia. However, bacterial infections can compromise fish health and growth performance, highlighting the need for natural feed additives that support sustainable aquaculture. Octopus (Octopus sp.) ink, a fishery by-product containing nutrients and bioactive compounds with potential antioxidant and antimicrobial properties, represents a promising alternative. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of octopus ink extract as a natural feed additive in improving the growth performance of catfish challenged with Staphylococcus aureus. A 50-day experiment was conducted using a completely randomized design with five treatments and three replicates. The treatments comprised K+ (infected fish without extract), K− (uninfected fish without extract), and three extract supplementation levels: A (25 mL/kg feed), B (50 mL/kg feed), and C (75 mL/kg feed), with all supplemented groups subjected to bacterial infection. Growth performance was assessed through absolute weight gain, absolute length gain, specific weight growth rate, and specific length growth rate. Octopus ink extract supplementation significantly affected growth performance (P < 0.05). Treatment C produced the highest absolute weight gain (8.50 ± 0.06 g), absolute length gain (5.18 ± 0.33 cm), and specific length growth rate (1.27 ± 0.07%/day), whereas treatment B achieved the highest specific weight growth rate (2.75 ± 0.14%/day). These findings suggest that octopus ink extract has potential as a natural feed additive for catfish, with 75 mL/kg feed providing the most favorable overall growth performance under the experimental conditions.

title: Tephra fall hazard and exposure analysis at corbetti volcanic system, Ethiopia: implications for risk management
abstractText: Abstract The Corbetti volcanic system, located in the central part of the Main Ethiopian Rift, has no recorded eruptions in living memory but shows evidence of past activity ranging from highly explosive Plinian eruptions to dominantly effusive events. Approximately 1.1 million people live within 30 km of the volcano and over 12 million within 100 km, alongside critical infrastructure such as highways, Hawassa Airport, and major towns including Hawassa and Shashemene. A geothermal power plant is also under development within the caldera. Despite significant advances in understanding Corbetti through recent fieldwork, hazard assessment remains limited due to challenges in distinguishing deposits, poor lateral continuity, and scarce dateable material. This study combines new and existing field data with expert judgment to develop probabilistic tephra-fall footprints for four plausible eruption scenarios and a worst-case scenario. These are integrated with exposure data to assess potential impacts and eruption frequency. Results indicate an average recurrence interval of 520 years for any explosive eruption, with low-to-moderate volume events ten times more likely than large Plinian eruptions. Modelling shows tephra dispersal predominantly westward, potentially exposing over 750,000 people, ~3,400 km of roads, and ~1,600 km 2 of cropland to tephra loads exceeding 1 kg m − 2 (~1.6 mm) during a Plinian-type event. In the same scenario, more than 37,000 people could experience > 100 kg m − 2 (~16 cm) of tephra within 20 km of the vent. Even smaller eruptions could significantly impact agriculture and infrastructure, underscoring the need for preparedness and risk management in a region with no historical memory of explosive volcanism.

title: Transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming during androgenesis in Brassica Rapa
Applying the Nedelsky Method to Determine Passing Scores for End-of-Course Examinations in Dentistry
abstractText: This research establishes a scientifically defensible passing score for the Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology final examination for dental students at Van Lang University by using the Nedelsky method. Five experts independently reviewed a 50-item multiple-choice test to identify distractors that a minimally competent candidate (MCC) could reasonably eliminate. The Minimum Passing Level (MPL) was calculated by averaging these expert estimates and subsequently applied to the examination results of 132 students. Student scores followed a normal distribution (p = 0.525), with an overall mean of 5.4 ± 1.3. The panel established an MPL of 52.4%, requiring at least 27 correct answers to pass. Compared to arbitrary fixed thresholds of 40% and 50%, the student pass rate decreased from 87.9% and 67.4%, respectively, to 52.3%. Twenty students - 15.2% of the cohort and 22.5% of those passing under the 50% threshold - were reclassified as borderline, indicating that they did not meet the competence level expected by the expert panel. The Nedelsky method created a higher passing standard based on student competence rather than convention. These results support adopting criterion-referenced methods to ensure assessments are fair and consistent with competency-based dental education.
